### **Game Rules**

1. Runs must have video footage with game audio, and must be at a minimum of 15fps on average (infrequent dips are fine)
2. For verification purposes, recordings must start on the main menu or otherwise a few seconds before the run has started
3. Runs must be performed on a vanilla version of the game with no modifications
4. Runners must have the following HUD elements unobstructed throughout the entire run: Health, Armor, and Fuel
5. You may not use any kind of Trainer, Cheat Table, Macro/Turbo, or otherwise unapproved external tools during runs. A Macro could include automated actions assigned to a single binding, or multiple actions bound to a single binding
6. External software such as RTSS or Nvidia control panel can be used to cap the framerate for stability purposes, but the cap must be in place for the entire run at the same value.

### **Category**

### **All Arenas**

Arenas are rooms where progression is halted until all enemies are defeated - marked by red doors sealing both entry and exit. Runners should take note that outside of arenas, **skipping other areas or enemies is allowed.**

1. Start with a new file and complete the demo (the use of Restart Mission while on Mission 0: Crash Course is permitted)
2. All arenas must be beaten by means of combat
3. Runners are permitted to play on any difficulty of their choosing
4. Runners are permitted to make use of all game mechanics and including exploits/skips/glitches with the exception of skips that rely on pause buffering to load/deload parts of the level (even if it loads fast enough on some hardware to not require pause buffering)
5. Intentionally lowering the in-game framerate, such as with the use of third-party software, is strictly prohibited

### **Timing**

1. Time starts on the first frame after leaving the Mission 0: Crash Course "Press any button to start" screen
2. Time ends on the first frame of the results screen appearing after completing Mission 1: Paradise Lost
3. Runs on the PC platform are required to use the LiveSplit load remover available within Livesplit under Edit Game so long as the game name is set as Metal Eden. You may download LiveSplit at[ http://livesplit.org/downloads/](http://livesplit.org/downloads/).
4. Runs on other platforms will be timed via Real-Time Attack (RTA)

- To aid verification, when recording your run, after you collect all the helmets in the game, quit to menu and **navigate to Mission Select to make the total helmet count visible**.
- Runners are also encouraged to show collected helmets (none) before starting a run, but this is not strictly required.
- **For those participating on console** if your run would be eligible for a cash prize but isn't due to load times or NCS time differences, **your final personal best run will be retimed at the end of the challenge during the verification phase**.

# **Timing**

- Timing begins after loading into the Gauntlet.
- Timing ends when you collect the last available helmet in the game.
- Run timing is done LRT (Load-Removed Time)
- If on PC, please use the load removal integration with LiveSplit.

## ***Bans & Restrictions***

### **- Glitches performed outside of the campaign**

This applies to 500% Core, Health, 2.5x damage, or any other glitch acquired outside of a run setting, most typically from a multiplayer private match. ***Any% Core Glitch is exempt from 500% Core and Health glitch restrictions.***

### **- Macros**

Any software or hardware used to input more actions than you would normally be able to do with a single input.

### **- Modification of in-game files**

This includes launching the game via icepick, vpk mods, and any other imaginable form of modification. For a whitelist of accepted custom.cfg and launch option commands,[ CLICK HERE!](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1lWE6VqNuvfi9ChKn4vdUHF5FF0B58bm9N_KiuOF2588/edit?usp=sharing)

### **-[ Zweek's Speedrun Menu Mod](https://www.speedrun.com/titanfall_2/resources/pf576) is excluded from the above rule and is allowed (but not required)**

### **- Digital to Analogue or Analogue to Digital Input Emulation (DA/ADIE)**

Digital and analogue inputs may not be emulated as their counterparts under any circumstances. Examples include software that emulates WASD directional inputs as analogue stick presses, or hardware like the XIM adapter for consoles. Compatibility software that allows for a variety of controllers to be used on PC, such as InputMapper or DS4Windows are acceptable, as they don't change the received input type (Analogue -> Analogue). Using software to bind controller D-Pads to WASD inputs is also accepted, as they don't change received input type (Digital -> Digital).

### **- Every bound key on your keyboard must be digital and have a set actuation point and release point**

Any keyboard that by design deviates from this default behavior is banned. For example, Wooting keyboards are not allowed due to their analog keypress and rapid trigger functionalities.

### **- Changing languages during a run is not permitted.**

### **- Max FPS must be capped between 30 and 144.**

# **High Profile Submission Requirements**

**High Profile runs are currently defined as runs with a leaderboard position in the top 5.**

- Full game audio. No segments of your run may be lacking clear game audio or muted. This does not mean you can't talk or play music during your run. Game audio must simply be easy to hear. If there's a problem with your audio, contact a moderator in discord for review.

- Input Overlay. PC runs (controller or keyboard) must have a visible input overlay at all times. Any overlay that clearly displays movement, crouch, and jump inputs is acceptable. Overlays can be found under the Resources tab. Console runs are exempt from this clause.

# **General Guide**

These aren't strict rules, but a list of general instructions if you're not sure how to get started with this category.

- To see all the helmet locations, we recommend watching an All Helmets or All Helmets NCS run that is already on the boards.

- Helmet collection persists when loading checkpoints, saves, and quitting to menu. These instructions take advantage of this. After collecting all the helmets in a level, you may immediately quit to menu and head for the next one, or use an NCS save to skip needless intro cutscenes.

# **NCS Installation Guide**

NCS Saves Download:[ https://www.speedrun.com/titanfall_2/resources](https://www.speedrun.com/titanfall_2/resources)

## **Pilot's Gauntlet**

After going through most of the gauntlet and collecting the helmet at the end, you may immediately load the "fastany1" save to start BT-7274 much faster than waiting for the cutscenes.

## **BT-7274**

You will need to do the first battery segment as usual, as you receive your double jump halfway through it. After returning to BT, you can either do the second battery segment normally, or directly head for the helmet by going right of the usual route, watching out for the unclimbable rocks on your way there. After collecting the second helmet, you may immediately quit to menu and load Blood and Rust from Mission Select.

## **Effect and Cause**

You can skip doing Chapter 1 of this level, as it takes about a minute to reach the helmet locations, you may instead start from Chapter 2, and upon getting all the helmets there, load chapter 3 and immediately head to the left from the building exit to find the last two helmets for this level.

## **The Beacon**

Again, skip chapter 1 and go directly for Beacon 2. After collecting the last helmet there, load the "fastany5" or "fasthelms5" save that takes you either directly into the fastball sequence or just before it in Beacon 3. Here, you can skip grabbing the module, and instead just do one big round trip to grab all 9 helmets in the level.

## **Trial by Fire**

Skip a short intro cutscene by loading the "fastany6" save. For the last helmet, it is possible to do a semi-precise climb to skip the elevator sequence to directly collect the helmet and load the next level.

## **The Ark & The Fold Weapon**

Both of these levels begin with pretty long intro cutscenes, so use the "fastany7" and "fastany8" saves respectively for each level when you're done with the previous one.

## Run Overview:

- The game is **Another Crab’s Treasure**
- The run will be **Any% | Restricted | (V1.0.102.0+) Same as Gamepass**
- Runs may be performed on either the Steam or PC Gamepass versions of the game, but not Console.
- Runs must start from the Title Screen, with the Patch number visibly shown

## Category Rules

In Restricted runs, the following glitches are banned:

- Uppies (infinite jump glitch) 
- Any form of up-warp or zip with a hammer charge attack (eg, Tissue Hammer) 
- Infinite Grapple glitch 
- Any form of unintended invulnerability (including permanent dodgeroll invulnerability in the Firth fight) 
- Infinite Crystal glitch abuse 
- Deloading zones to bypass terrain

Some examples of skips, glitches, and tech that are explicitly allowed:

- Any form of boss skip, regardless of whether or not the boss healthbar spawns in (eg; Camtscha skip, Inkerton skip) 
- Clipping through walls, including level OoB invisible walls, by entering a shell behind them 
- Depression Skip (gaining early full control of Kril after defeating Roland) 
- Instantly killing bosses by baiting them off cliffs 
- Walking on inter-level OoB geometry (eg, Voltai Early) 
- Charged Attack Launches

## Challenge Submission Requirements

- Runs must be **streamed on Twitch / YouTube** / other streaming services in order to be valid for the competition. If not streamed, runs may still be submitted, but will not be eligible for the prize pool.
    - Video proof **must be permanent** (i.e. Twitch Highlight / Youtube Video)
    - All **HUD elements** (bottom corners / boss HP bars) **must be unobstructed** during gameplay
    - Runs must have audio that is audible and noticeable. This means that **in-game sound FX** must be on. In-game music is optional. If audio is muted due to music or other reasons, those runs will not be accepted.
- Runs must use the **Autosplitter / Load Remover** that is found in LiveSplit.
- Runs must use an **input display** containing all inputs used. Can be any, the most common are these two:
    - **Nohboard** for KBM input.
    - **Gamepadviewer** for controller.
- FPS must be **capped at 60 FPS**.
    - Steam FPS overlay, Rivatuner, Microsoft Game Bar etc. should work fine.
    - There is no soft cap, runs must stay at the 60 FPS that is specified.
- [Automash mod ](https://www.speedrun.com/Another_Crabs_Treasure/resources/at991)on Speedrun.com is allowed. It will be the only macro allowed for the competition.
- Multibinds are allowed as long as they are configured in-game.
- ControlMapping.usersettings.xml is the only allowed edited game file for additional binds. Altering game files in any other way is not allowed.
- Assist Mode is strictly prohibited from the run.

# Timing

- Unless specified otherwise, runs are ranked by loadless time, achieved by using an autosplitter and load remover integrated with LiveSplit. (Make sure to set Compare Against to "Game Time", and make sure you open LiveSplit *after* the game is open to the main menu.)
- If not load removing, or if your LiveSplit with load remover is not clearly visible for the whole run, your real time with loads will be used instead.
- Pausing the timer manually will lead to all the time while paused (real time) being added to your final time.

- You must complete all secret levels and finish the game (Prime Sanctums are not included)

- Time starts on entering the 1st level.

- Time ends when finishing the last currently available level and reaching the level completion screen. (currently 7-4)

- Taking a secret exit means you must complete the secret level.

- Taking an exit to a level that loops back means you **must** complete the main level again.

- Getting a false level finish means you must re-start the level. (hitting the trigger at the end of a level from out of bounds in such a way that the mission complete screen appears but you can't click to continue)

# **General Rules**

> *The following rules apply to all categories* unless specified *otherwise* in the category's rules.

1. All categories are run NG+.
2. All runs must start the first level in the category and play through every level, *without quitting out*, until the last level in the category is finished. The only exception to this rule is between acts, *after clicking past the Mission Complete screen for the last level in the act,* runners may quit out and start the first level in the next act on the same difficulty in order to save time, clicks, and sanity.
3. All runs are sorted by In-Game Time by default. Runners may also include Real Time Attack (Time) for full-game categories only.

    - IGT is determined by adding the end time for every level as well as the time spent in a level before a full level reset. There is an excel document in the resources tab to help do this; However, it is not required to use this method.
    - RTA is timed from the first frame after the first level finishes loading to the frame the HUD disappears when exiting the last level of the category.

4. The entire Mission Completion screen must be shown for every level for proof of level completion. This must be done even if the In-Game Timer stops before entering the end pipe for the last level in the category.
5. The intent of the run must be to speedrun the category. Joke runs, walk-throughs, and runs featuring a self-imposed challenge will be rejected.

# **Cheats**

1. Cheats and Major Assists must be **disabled** unless specified otherwise.
2. Auto Aim must be **disabled**.
3. Use of the developer console is **not** allowed.
4. Viewing and/or editing memory values with any program other than the autosplitter is **not** allowed.
5. Modifications or additions to the game's files are **not** allowed. This includes but is not limited to Reshade, Texture mods, and BepInEx (even if no other mods are installed).
6. Binding keys through a program outside of the game itself is **not** allowed. This includes but is not limited to the use of macros or auto clickers.
7. Abuse of peripherals that provide a distinct advantage is **not** allowed. This includes but is not limited to free spin mouse wheels, double clicking mice, and Turbo buttons.
8. Segmented/Spliced runs are **not** allowed on the leaderboard.
9. Site bans will be issued if necessary.

# **Relevant Glitches and Exploits**

1. False Level Finish – Hitting the end of level trigger from out of bounds in such a way that the Mission Complete screen appears but you cannot click to continue.

    - Not acceptable for multi-level runs. Runners must restart the level using the menu.
    - Acceptable for individual-level runs.

2. Glitches or exploits that cause the in-game timer to not count properly or cause it to not start are **not** allowed.
3. Clipping out of the level start room (even after the timer has started) is **not** allowed.
4. Before the timer has started, stacking sources of infinite damage, i.e. deadcoining or chainsaw stacking, is **not** allowed.
5. In an effort to keep things from being patchlocked immediately, any tech or strategies removed on or before patch 16c are banned for post-revamp runs.

# **Video Requirements**

1. All runs require video proof.
2. Video must contain the entirety of the run from before the first level loads to after the last level is completed, with the entire final Mission Completion screen clearly shown.
3. Video must be of a viewable quality and without excessive graphics settings for the entirety of the run, up to the discretion of the verifiers. (Excessive graphics settings includes post processing effects, such as motion blur.)
4. Videos or images covering a majority of the screen, or the HUD/other important areas are **not** allowed.
5. Inappropriate/offensive language or imagery in the video/thumbnail are **not** allowed.
6. It is recommended that the game audio is clearly audible in the video.
7. It is recommended to have some form of on-screen timer throughout the video. The best ways to do this are either to have the Tab menu open or to use LiveSplit.
8. Videos must be uploaded to a persistent video sharing site like YouTube, Twitch clips (Not highlights), or BiliBili. Videos submitted through a site that does not embed natively on SRC will likely be rejected.

# **Submission Requirements**

1. Please make sure all submission fields are correct before submitting.
2. Uploading runs from other runners is **not** allowed.
3. When submitting Individual Level runs, please **only submit ‘In-Game Time’** and leave the ‘Time’ field blank.
4. Video must meet all Video Requirements.
5. Runs must meet all other requirements for the game and category being submitted to.
6. Runs done on the demo version are **not** allowed. Please check the category rules for acceptable versions per category.
7. Submissions must follow all other site rules.
8. Please wait at least 14 days prior to contacting the moderators regarding the status of a pending run. Keep in mind that there is often a high influx of runs, and that verifiers are volunteers.
9. When submitting multiple run improvements, please create a new submission rather than editing an old submission in order to maintain the history of runs in the database.

# **Additional Requirements**

Top 10 Times require the following:

- Clearly audible in-game audio.
- Tab menu open for the entire run. (double tap tab)
- Steam Overlay's in-game FPS counter enabled and visible for the entire run, preferably with high contrast.

If using OBS' game capture, ensure 'Capture third party overlays' is enabled in properties for FPS to appear in the recording. If having trouble with Steam Overlay disappearing, try running Steam as administrator.

Moderators may impart extra submission requirements or offer lessened submission requirements on a case-by-case basis.

You are not permitted to take extended breaks during the run when the in-game timer is paused without a valid reason. For example, time taken to load the save file after a crash or between bosses in Boss Rush.
The acceptance of such breaks is at the moderators' discretion, based on factors such as the break's duration, total run time, and the validity of the reason provided.

gameList.name: Doom (Kex Port)
gameList.rules:
### NOTE: 

Previously, due to a glitch that affected enemy aggro, loading a save was prohibited for full game runs. However, this glitch has since been patched. As such, **loading a save on Solo Full Game runs is allowed**. Effective 10/3/2024, 1:10 PM.

# **Solo Full Game Runs**

- Timing starts on the frame after final menu selection.
- Timing ends on first frame of the screen melt on the final level.
- Death starts are NOT allowed.
- All full game runs MUST show the results screen in full at the end of map 8/map 30. If only the melt is shown, and no results screen, moderators may reject or verify at their own discretion.
- For top 5 Solo Full Game submissions, sound effects audio **MUST** be present and at a reasonable level.
- For top 5 Solo Full Game submissions, the player **MUST** have screen flash effects toggled ON.

# **Co-Op Full Game Runs**

- Timing starts on the first frame that the host has loaded into the level.
- Timing ends on the first frame that the host sees the final intermission screen.
- Death starts are NOT allowed.
- Toggling the Modern Co-Op feature is allowed.
- Runs with two players are expected to provide both points of view for verification. Without both POVs, moderators may reject your run at their discretion.
- Runs with three or four players are BOTH expected to provide at least three points of view for verification. Without at least three points of view, moderators may reject your run at their discretion.
- For top 3 Co-Op run submissions, the host **MUST** have screen flash effects toggled ON.

# **Solo Individual Level Rules**

- The level must either be started via the level select menu, or through any other technique specifically described below.
- In the event there is no results screen for the given level, timing starts on first available input, and ends on first frame of screen melt.
- Quick saving just before a death, and quick loading the IL for Any% and NoMonsters is accepted. Similarly, dying and restarting the IL for Any% and NoMonsters is accepted.
- Accidental quick saves during any IL are NOT allowed.
- Pausing during any IL is NOT allowed.
- When loading into the level, the initial screen melt must be shown ***in full***.
- For Solo IL record submissions, the player **MUST** have screen flash effects toggled ON.

# **Co-Op Individual Level Rules**

- The level must be started via the level select menu. Death starts are NOT allowed for any Co-Op IL category. 
- Runs with two players are expected to provide both points of view for verification. Without both POVs, moderators may reject your run at their discretion.
- Respawning after death is NOT allowed for any player.
- Toggling the Modern Co-Op feature is *discouraged*. With this feature toggled, dead players may respawn automatically, so use this feature at your own risk.
- For Co-Op IL record submissions, the host **MUST** have screen flash effects toggled ON.
- NOTE FOR UV-MAX: The Co-Op intermission screen only tracks kills performed by each player - enemies that died via infighting are not accounted for. As such, it is **highly recommended** that at least one player opens their minimap at the end of the run so that we can more easily verify that max kills has been achieved.

# **General Submission Rules**

# 

- If runs being submitted to the leaderboard have commentary, it must follow TOS standards for most public access forums like Twitch. Submissions that have racial/sexist/hate commentary, visible/horrific imagery, or offensive materials to the general public, will result in a rejection.
- **Runs of any kind MUST show the messages in the top left in full**. If they are covered in any way, moderators may reject your run at their discretion. **This also goes for anything on the HUD**, whether it's your Health, Armor, Ammo count, etc. They are not to be covered.
- Toggling "Use Multiplayer Items", "No Monsters", "Fast Monsters", or "Monsters Respawn" in the level select menu is NOT allowed, with the exception of "No Monsters" for the NoMonsters category.
- For Co-Op runs, 2 or more players are **REQUIRED.** Further, plugging input devices in and leaving them motionless, or 1 person on two or more controllers, is **NOT ALLOWED.**
- Video submission is required for **ALL** runs.

gameList.name: ULTRAKILL
gameList.rules:
# **General Rules**

> *The following rules apply to all categories* unless specified *otherwise* in the category's rules.

1. All categories are run NG+.
2. All runs must start the first level in the category and play through every level, *without quitting out*, until the last level in the category is finished. The only exception to this rule is between acts, *after clicking past the Mission Complete screen for the last level in the act,* runners may quit out and start the first level in the next act on the same difficulty in order to save time, clicks, and sanity.
3. All runs are sorted by In-Game Time by default. Runners may also include Real Time Attack (Time) for full-game categories only.

    - IGT is determined by adding the end time for every level as well as the time spent in a level before a full level reset. There is an excel document in the resources tab to help do this; However, it is not required to use this method.
    - RTA is timed from the first frame after the first level finishes loading to the frame the HUD disappears when exiting the last level of the category.

4. The entire Mission Completion screen must be shown for every level for proof of level completion. This must be done even if the In-Game Timer stops before entering the end pipe for the last level in the category.
5. The intent of the run must be to speedrun the category. Joke runs, walk-throughs, and runs featuring a self-imposed challenge will be rejected.

# **Cheats**

1. Cheats and Major Assists must be **disabled** unless specified otherwise.
2. Auto Aim must be **disabled**.
3. Use of the developer console is **not** allowed.
4. Viewing and/or editing memory values with any program other than the autosplitter is **not** allowed.
5. Modifications or additions to the game's files are **not** allowed. This includes but is not limited to Reshade, Texture mods, and BepInEx (even if no other mods are installed).
6. Binding keys through a program outside of the game itself is **not** allowed. This includes but is not limited to the use of macros or auto clickers.
7. Abuse of peripherals that provide a distinct advantage is **not** allowed. This includes but is not limited to free spin mouse wheels, double clicking mice, and Turbo buttons.
8. Segmented/Spliced runs are **not** allowed on the leaderboard.
9. Site bans will be issued if necessary.

# **Relevant Glitches and Exploits**

1. False Level Finish – Hitting the end of level trigger from out of bounds in such a way that the Mission Complete screen appears but you cannot click to continue.

    - Not acceptable for multi-level runs. Runners must restart the level using the menu.
    - Acceptable for individual-level runs.

2. Glitches or exploits that cause the in-game timer to not count properly or cause it to not start are **not** allowed.
3. Clipping out of the level start room (even after the timer has started) is **not** allowed.
4. Before the timer has started, stacking sources of infinite damage, i.e. deadcoining or chainsaw stacking, is **not** allowed.
5. In an effort to keep things from being patchlocked immediately, any tech or strategies removed on or before patch 16c are banned for post-revamp runs.

# **Video Requirements**

1. All runs require video proof.
2. Video must contain the entirety of the run from before the first level loads to after the last level is completed, with the entire final Mission Completion screen clearly shown.
3. Video must be of a viewable quality and without excessive graphics settings for the entirety of the run, up to the discretion of the verifiers. (Excessive graphics settings includes post processing effects, such as motion blur.)
4. Videos or images covering a majority of the screen, or the HUD/other important areas are **not** allowed.
5. Inappropriate/offensive language or imagery in the video/thumbnail are **not** allowed.
6. It is recommended that the game audio is clearly audible in the video.
7. It is recommended to have some form of on-screen timer throughout the video. The best ways to do this are either to have the Tab menu open or to use LiveSplit.
8. Videos must be uploaded to a persistent video sharing site like YouTube, Twitch clips (Not highlights), or BiliBili. Videos submitted through a site that does not embed natively on SRC will likely be rejected.

# **Submission Requirements**

1. Please make sure all submission fields are correct before submitting.
2. Uploading runs from other runners is **not** allowed.
3. When submitting Individual Level runs, please **only submit ‘In-Game Time’** and leave the ‘Time’ field blank.
4. Video must meet all Video Requirements.
5. Runs must meet all other requirements for the game and category being submitted to.
6. Runs done on the demo version are **not** allowed. Please check the category rules for acceptable versions per category.
7. Submissions must follow all other site rules.
8. Please wait at least 14 days prior to contacting the moderators regarding the status of a pending run. Keep in mind that there is often a high influx of runs, and that verifiers are volunteers.
9. When submitting multiple run improvements, please create a new submission rather than editing an old submission in order to maintain the history of runs in the database.

# **Additional Requirements**

Top 10 Times require the following:

- Clearly audible in-game audio.
- Tab menu open for the entire run. (double tap tab)
- Steam Overlay's in-game FPS counter enabled and visible for the entire run, preferably with high contrast.

If using OBS' game capture, ensure 'Capture third party overlays' is enabled in properties for FPS to appear in the recording. If having trouble with Steam Overlay disappearing, try running Steam as administrator.

Moderators may impart extra submission requirements or offer lessened submission requirements on a case-by-case basis.

gameList.name: Celeste
gameList.rules:
## General Game Rules
* Timing is done using the in-game timer, please refrain from taking long breaks mid-run.
* Closing the game during the run is banned. This includes crashes.
* Entering a level in another save file during the run is banned.
* Using cheat mode, having assist or variant mode enabled, or using debug mode features during the run are banned.
* Altering any game files except for *settings.celeste* is banned. In particular, runs done on Everest are not allowed. You can restart into vanilla Celeste by holding right on the title screen.
* The use of any third-party programs that directly affect the game are banned, with the exception of keyboard rebinders, controller mappers, and autosplitters.

## Verification Requirements
* All runs require permanent video proof.
* All Full-game runs should either have File timer enabled or show the exact File time on Livesplit using the autosplitter. Make sure that all digits down to the hundredths (.00) are clearly visible for the entire run.
* The game version must be shown on either the title screen or a chapter complete screen while using an in-game timer.
* For Full-game runs, the final in-game time must be verified either by showing:
   * The pie screen in Epilogue
   * The file on the file selection screen
   * The journal
   * The final chapter complete screen while using the File timer.
* When submitting your run, leave *Time* blank and only fill in *In-game time*.  Make sure to also include the 3 decimal digits.
* Throughout the run, please refrain from obstructing the following sections of the screen with your overlay (including: input displays, PNGs, alert notifications, etc.) If for any reason these areas are not visible, your run will be rejected: https://imgur.com/a/pFKo3Ni

## Additional Proof Requirements

For the following submissions to this leaderboard, players must be able to provide a session recording with unedited audio:
* Top 3 Any%
* Top 3 1A, 2A, and 5B Clear
* World Record in all other full game/IL categories
See our FAQ for more information: https://tinyurl.com/celesteProofcall

## Submission Recommendations
The following bullet points are not mandatory for most submissions, but high level runs that fail to adhere to any of them will likely require the runner to provide additional proof to moderators. If this cannot be done, the run may be rejected. Repeat instances will be treated more harshly.

* Have clearly audible game sounds in your video proof.
* Unless you are on the chapter select screen, avoid tabbing out of the game while playing in Fullscreen mode, as this freezes the game feed during sections that are relevant for verification.
* For fullgame runs, include the file creation in your video proof.

Note that while in-game sound is not required for most submissions, if your video does not have sound and has significant amounts of dropped frames, stuttering, or cuts from tabbing out of the game, it cannot be verified.

## Patch Restriction
* The run must be performed on the newest patch available on the platform you use at time of play. Beta patches are not allowed.
* Any exploits that are not possible to perform on the most up-to-date PC patch are banned.

gameList.name: Minecraft: Java Edition
gameList.rules:
**The following is a heavily abridged summary of the rules. To view the full rules, please click [here.](https://www.minecraftspeedrunning.com/public-resources/rules) This is only intended to be a user-friendly version of the rules which highlights key details and rules which must be followed. In addition to reading these rules, it is highly recommended to watch the [official submission guide](https://youtu.be/z2n2fCV1GY0) when submitting runs.**

# **Important Reminders**

**The F3 screen must be shown in the video of the run for all runs.**

- You still need to show F3 after the run is over even if you don’t use it in the run. (such as No F3 categories)
- When you show the F3 screen, make sure all parts are legible and unobscured.

**All runs must be submitted with a video.**

- The video must be permanent and viewable. (no Twitch VODs or private videos)

**You must include the world seed in your submission description.**

**Runs must include a video that shows all screens of creating the world, followed by the loading square.**

- For vanilla runs, you must show the World List and Create New World screens. If the run is set seed, you must also show the Seed Input screen.
- For runs that use the Atum mod, the video must show part of the prior run and the world generation loading square. 
- If you are using the mods Atum and SpeedrunIGT, and the SpeedrunIGT timer is visible upon the run’s start, and the F3 screen is opened and visible before exiting the world, the video does not need to include any world generation.

**Recreate is banned in versions 1.16+ for set seed runs.**

# **Mod Rules**

**Fabric API is banned.**

- This is a separate .jar file and not the Fabric Loader itself.

**Optifine is banned for 1.15+.**

- If you choose to use Optifine in pre-1.15, you may only do so with particular settings. These settings can be found in [A.8.1](https://github.com/Minecraft-Java-Edition-Speedrunning/rules/blob/132b6ffbbca78414626587b3f0d0331a3a04365e/rules.md?plain=1#L687) of the full rules. 

**Fabric Loader is the only allowed mod loader. Do not use Forge or anything else.**

**There are only a few mods that you are allowed to use, which can be found here ([https://mods.tildejustin.dev/](https://mods.tildejustin.dev/)).**

- We recommend using SpeedrunIGT for ease of verification.

# **General Speedrun Rules**

**Keep the default settings of world generation.**

- You can only change the world name, difficulty (except for Peaceful), or choosing hardcore instead of survival.

**Do not edit the game’s files.**

- However, in the options.txt file, gamma may be edited up to 5.0.
- A launcher which has been verified to leave the game unmodified must be used. This includes:
  - The vanilla Minecraft launcher
  - MultiMC
  - Prism Launcher

**Do not use commands during the run.**

**Do not use Peaceful difficulty during the run.**

**The way runs are timed is either by world load or by first input, depending upon the category.**

**Runs must not intend to be as slow as possible (no “slowruns”).**

# **Submission Rules**

**Mark your run as F3 if it uses the F3 screen during the run, or any feature which is triggered by an F3 hotkey (such as F3+B hitboxes, F3+H advanced tooltips or F3+Esc pausing).**

**Mark your run’s difficulty as the lowest difficulty played during the run.**

**Mark the mods section of your run in accordance with the mods you used at any point during the run.**

- If no mods are used, choose Vanilla.
- If just Optifine (not Optifabric) is used, choose Optifine.
- If anything else (including Optifabric, Fabric Loader) is used, choose Modded.

# **Resource Pack Rules**

**You are only allowed to use a few resource packs. If you want to be safe, just use the vanilla resource pack.**

- You can use any vanilla resource packs, including the default pack, Programmer Art, and High Contrast packs.
- Detailed resource pack rules can be found in section A.4 of the full rules.
- If you use a non-vanilla resource pack, include a link to it in the speedrun.com run’s description.

# **Additional Proof**

**When submitting additional proof, please use the official Google form (**[https://forms.gle/v7oPXfjfi7553jkp7](https://forms.gle/v7oPXfjfi7553jkp7)**).**

**Additional proof is only required for achieving certain times in certain categories (see category rules to see if you need to). Regardless, when submitting a run, you agree to provide extra proof if asked by moderators. Refusal may lead to rejection.**

**If you are unsure how to submit certain pieces of additional proof, please follow the [tutorial](https://youtu.be/z2n2fCV1GY0) on submitting additional proof.**

# **External Tool Rules**

**SeedQueue, a mod that simulates multi-instance, where multiple instances of Minecraft are used to reset faster, is recommended in versions where it is available.**

- If you want to use multiple instances, such as in versions where SeedQueue is not available, please read the detailed multiple instance rules in section A.9 of the full rules.

**If you open multiple instances of Minecraft, they must each be in unique directories (separate .minecraft folders).**

**Do not use any macros in-game except for resize macros.**

- Any macros which change the screen size to within the monitor bounds may be used.
- Only one macro may make the game window larger than the monitor size, like a zoom macro for measuring Eyes of Ender. (intended to replace above rule)

**You may remap keys using external programs (like AutoHotkey), but it must be a one-to-one remap.**

- For instance, Shift+F3 cannot be rebound to a singular key.
- You may not rebind anything to the scrolling action of the scroll wheel.

**Physical reference sheets may be used, as well as four-function calculators. A reference sheet of any size not based on F3 information may be used.**

- For instance, stronghold ring locations, sheets/graphs of structure regions, and villager trading tables may be used.

**Other reference sheets and external tools must be specifically approved to be used as listed in [A.11.6 and A.11.7](https://github.com/Minecraft-Java-Edition-Speedrunning/rules/blob/132b6ffbbca78414626587b3f0d0331a3a04365e/rules.md?plain=1#L827) of the full rules.**

**Specifically approved external tools may be used, as listed in [A.11.7](https://github.com/Minecraft-Java-Edition-Speedrunning/rules/blob/132b6ffbbca78414626587b3f0d0331a3a04365e/rules.md?plain=1#L835) of the full rules. All other external tools may not be used.**

- Ninjabrain Bot for measuring Eyes of Ender is allowed.

# **Random Seed Rules**

**You are required to use a random seed (leave the seed input box blank).**

**You may not learn the seed during the run.**

- Do not do /seed until the run is over.
- Do not attempt to crack the world seed.
- After the run you should do /seed in order to include the seed in your run submission.
- Do not use F3 in pre-1.3 (it shows the seed).

# **Set Seed Rules**

**Recreate is banned in versions 1.16+.**

**You are required to set a world seed.**

# **Glitchless Rules**

**Do not save and quit or leave the game during the run.**

- You can save and quit accidentally or to resolve a bug. See the detailed rules on using Save and Quit in glitchless runs to see under what conditions it is allowed in D.1.3 of the full rules.

**A few additional techniques can be used in glitchless runs.**

- These include double-eating and Eliotex sprinting. See the detailed rules on what techniques are and aren’t allowed for glitchless runs in D.1.1 and D.1.2 of the full rules.

**SSG and RSG stand for “Set Seed Glitchless” and “Random Seed Glitchless” respectively, so they must follow the rules above.**

# **Glitched Rules**

**Glitched runs must use at least one glitch.**

- In External categories, you may Save and Quit and crash the game.

**It is highly recommended to use SpeedrunIGT in glitched categories, going to Timer, and setting the Autosave Interval to Ticks.**

**All gameplay segments are timed in glitched runs.**

**Any categories without the word “Glitchless” are glitched. This includes Any%, SS, and RS.**

# **Co-op Rules**

**Use either a dedicated** **server or Open to LAN.**

**Your server cannot use any mods that are banned, even if there are no plugins.**

- Do not use Paper, Spigot, CraftBukkit, or Bungeecord.

**You can use /difficulty to change the difficulty.**

- Do not change the difficulty in options, as it will enable peaceful momentarily.
- You must enable cheats to do this.

**If all players wait until everyone has joined, one person can do /time set 0, which will start the run’s timer.**

- You must enable cheats to do this.
- Do not use /time set 0 more than once.

**The first person to join the server, the person to complete the run, and anyone with cheats enabled must record their perspectives. When submitting your run, include these videos in the speedrun.com run description.**

- It is helpful to have all players submit a video, but only the ones above are required to.

**If more than 16 players are running, choose 16 players while submitting, input the names of 15 of the players, and then list “+others” for the 16th slot. Include the name of all other players not listed in the description of the speedrun.com submission.**

# **Structures/No Structures Rules**

**A structure is anything that requires Generate Structures: On to generate. (such as a Village, Nether Fortress, Mineshaft).**

- Dungeons are also considered a structure.
- See the full list of structures in [G.1.1](https://github.com/Minecraft-Java-Edition-Speedrunning/rules/blob/132b6ffbbca78414626587b3f0d0331a3a04365e/rules.md?plain=1#L1081) of the full rules.

**A category marked ‘Structures’ must use at least one structure.**

**A category marked ‘No Structures’ cannot use any structures.**

- You may choose Generate Structures: Off, or keep them on but do not interact with them.

gameList.name: Super Mario 64
gameList.rules:
**IMPORTANT:** To see specific rules for N64/VC/EMU subcategories, check the 'Category Rules' tab as well.

## Video Requirements:

All submissions requires a full video of the run, including game audio. 

## 

- The whole run should be in one segment
- Game audio must be audible (runs may be accepted with the 'Verified: No' flag for: extremely low game audio, constant music playback, and other related avoidable situations)
- The video link MUST embed on the run page (e.g. no URL shorteners or sketchy file sharing sites)
- VODs should persist indefinitely (e.g. Highlight instead of Past Broadcast)
- Dynamic HUD elements should not be obscured or omitted (e.g. coin count, star count, life count)

## Auto-rejection (SM64 Moderation Bot):

We use a bot to auto-reject runs which do not fill out the submission forms correctly, since we can't perform data validation via the submission form. If your run is auto-rejected, simply edit the submission with the fixes and resubmit the run. This has no bearing on the validity of your run (which may or may not be rejected for other reasons).

To avoid auto-rejection:

- Do not include milliseconds in your final time.
- Make sure the Platform matches the Platform subcategory (N64/VC/EMU)
- Make sure you highlight your twitch VOD.
- Leave the "Verified" flag set to "Yes"

## Good Faith Submissions

Runs are expected to be performed in good faith and may be rejected based on mod discretion if performed otherwise.  Examples include, but are not limited to: extended stalling to achieve a specific time; intentionally attempting to get the last place time on the leaderboard and/or the longest time possible; or attempting to exploit technicalities in the written category rules in a manner contrary to the spirit of the category. This means that long runs and/or runs with breaks will be considered in good faith so long as effort is still being made.

gameList.rules:
All runs require video proof (with audio).

It is recommended that every submitted video that includes Daylight Saving Time Abuse (DSTA) start by showing Daylight Saving Time (DST) being set prior to starting the run.

As of June 23rd, 2021 Switch FW versions older than 10.0 are prohibited. If a run happens to get *Fast Action Guide Skip*, please make sure to show your FW version after the run has finished.

Network System Clock Abuse (NSCA) is banned for all categories.

Runs must be done entirely with your switch in docked or undocked mode, you may not switch between the 2 mid-run.

Use of Amiibo, Luigi's Balloon World, and Assist Mode is banned.

Unless expressly stated otherwise, runs must be done in one-player mode only.

Runs performed on emulator will not be verified (switch hardware only).

**Breaks**

If your run uses breaks, choose TA for the Method variable. If it doesn't, choose RTA.

Both start and end of every break must be timestamped in the run description.

Breaks are only allowed during cutscenes; this includes moon animations.

When taking a break, runners should bring up the menu to edit the system time while synchronization with the internet is turned off. This is to ensure that enough time has passed outside of breaks for a seed to be fully grown and the moon to be collected. This option is under "Date and Time" in the switch settings menu. Make sure to confirm the system time with an "A" press at the end of your break so it remains the same as it was at the start of the break.

The pool of available time for breaks gains 15 minutes every 2 hours. Breaks can be taken at any point in the run, and there is no limit on the number of breaks so long as it follows the rules established above.

For example:

- Any run under 2 hours cannot take any breaks.

- Any run between 2 and 4 hours (2:00:00 - 3:59:59) has 15 minutes available for breaks.

- Any run between 4 and 6 hours (4:00:00 - 5:59:59) has 30 minutes available for breaks.

- etc.

Breaks are calculated based on the final run time, so if a runner knows that the run will be over 2 hours they can use from the 15 minute pool instantly. Should mistakes be made, and the run did not hit the required threshold to allow breaks (or did not hit the required threshold to use the amount of break time taken), the run will be retimed.

# Gameplay Rules

- [This Document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GTqbWx6_qfHnn_j4cJLdjcPcDBszOsKCXWPQLnFUxUg/edit?usp=sharing) covers all the information regarding currently allowed glitches/techniques/strats.
- You are not allowed to revive (besides endless categories).
- In multiplayer runs no one is allowed to become a ghost with the gamepass.
- You are not allowed to use any macros.
- Binding keys is allowed, with the exception of the scroll wheel and similar methods for key spamming.
- All in-game settings are allowed including Deaf Mode, with the exception of Free Cam.
- The developer console is allowed.
- No shaders are allowed, however display settings that are undetectable in recordings such as gamma are always allowed.

# Recording Rules

- **Audio is required for all runs** (except for multiplayer runs, where some POVs can not have audio).
- The assets and revive count must be visible throughout the whole run (if applicable).
- You must start your recording before pressing the "Skip Waiting" button in the submarine, or before the timer runs out.
- The run must be raw and unedited (the run must be uncut, however you are allowed to edit a timer or any captions in as long as the run is still clearly visible and the timer doesn't obstruct the kroner/revive area.)
- Your recording must be of acceptable quality (this is based on the discretion of verifiers.) Make sure to not use the Roblox video recorder. Shorter and more competitive categories may require higher framerate to ensure an accurate retime.
- Switching windows/tabs is allowed during your run, however you must be in the game at the start and end of the run.
- For Xbox runs that can only record videos up to 10 minutes, you are allowed to make multiple recordings of your game, and you must put all recordings together in the same videos. You cannot move or change your camera angle while you aren't recording, and there cannot be a entity coming while you aren't recording.

# Timing Rules

- The in-game timer is optional, but appreciated.
- The in-game timer is not the official time of the run. Runs are re-timed by moderators to determine the real time.
- The start/end times of runs can be found in Category Rules.

# Multiplayer Rules

- *All rules above still apply for all POVs.*
- If there are more than 20 players in the run, due to speedrun.com limitations, 21st participant and beyond must be mentioned inside the run's description.
- All POVs of players are required for Duo, Trio, and Squad runs. For 5-8 and 9+ player runs, only four POVs are required. To attach multiple clips in a single run submission, simply place all the links inside the video URL textbox, separating them with spaces (e.g., [https//:video1 https//:video2 https//:video3]).
- Deaths are allowed (except in All Alive% category), as long as the game is completed by at least 1 run participant with valid recording and no revives were used by anyone through out the whole run.
- If someone happens to die, they must keep on recording until their revive timer runs out.
- If someone happens to disconnect/leave, they must include that in the recording as well.

gameList.rules:
**The following is a heavily abridged summary of the rules. To view the full rules, please click [here.](https://www.minecraftspeedrunning.com/public-resources/rules) This is only intended to be a user-friendly version of the rules which highlights key details and rules which must be followed. In addition to reading these rules, it is highly recommended to watch the [official submission guide](https://youtu.be/z2n2fCV1GY0) when submitting runs.**

# **Important Reminders**

**The F3 screen must be shown in the video of the run for all runs.**

- You still need to show F3 after the run is over even if you don’t use it in the run. (such as No F3 categories)
- When you show the F3 screen, make sure all parts are legible and unobscured.

**All runs must be submitted with a video.**

- The video must be permanent and viewable. (no Twitch VODs or private videos)

**You must include the world seed in your submission description.**

**Runs must include a video that shows all screens of creating the world, followed by the loading square.**

- For vanilla runs, you must show the World List and Create New World screens. If the run is set seed, you must also show the Seed Input screen.
- For runs that use the Atum mod, the video must show part of the prior run and the world generation loading square. 
- If you are using the mods Atum and SpeedrunIGT, and the SpeedrunIGT timer is visible upon the run’s start, and the F3 screen is opened and visible before exiting the world, the video does not need to include any world generation.

**Recreate is banned in versions 1.16+ for set seed runs.**

# **Mod Rules**

**Fabric API is banned.**

- This is a separate .jar file and not the Fabric Loader itself.

**Optifine is banned for 1.15+.**

- If you choose to use Optifine in pre-1.15, you may only do so with particular settings. These settings can be found in [A.8.1](https://github.com/Minecraft-Java-Edition-Speedrunning/rules/blob/132b6ffbbca78414626587b3f0d0331a3a04365e/rules.md?plain=1#L687) of the full rules. 

**Fabric Loader is the only allowed mod loader. Do not use Forge or anything else.**

**There are only a few mods that you are allowed to use, which can be found here ([https://mods.tildejustin.dev/](https://mods.tildejustin.dev/)).**

- We recommend using SpeedrunIGT for ease of verification.

# **General Speedrun Rules**

**Keep the default settings of world generation.**

- You can only change the world name, difficulty (except for Peaceful), or choosing hardcore instead of survival.

**Do not edit the game’s files.**

- However, in the options.txt file, gamma may be edited up to 5.0.
- A launcher which has been verified to leave the game unmodified must be used. This includes:
  - The vanilla Minecraft launcher
  - MultiMC
  - Prism Launcher

**Do not use commands during the run.**

**Do not use Peaceful difficulty during the run.**

**The way runs are timed is either by world load or by first input, depending upon the category.**

**Runs must not intend to be as slow as possible (no “slowruns”).**

# **Submission Rules**

**Mark your run as F3 if it uses the F3 screen during the run, or any feature which is triggered by an F3 hotkey (such as F3+B hitboxes, F3+H advanced tooltips or F3+Esc pausing).**

**Mark your run’s difficulty as the lowest difficulty played during the run.**

**Mark the mods section of your run in accordance with the mods you used at any point during the run.**

- If no mods are used, choose Vanilla.
- If just Optifine (not Optifabric) is used, choose Optifine.
- If anything else (including Optifabric, Fabric Loader) is used, choose Modded.

# **Resource Pack Rules**

**You are only allowed to use a few resource packs. If you want to be safe, just use the vanilla resource pack.**

- You can use any vanilla resource packs, including the default pack, Programmer Art, and High Contrast packs.
- Detailed resource pack rules can be found in section A.4 of the full rules.
- If you use a non-vanilla resource pack, include a link to it in the speedrun.com run’s description.

# **Additional Proof**

**When submitting additional proof, please use the official Google form (**[https://forms.gle/v7oPXfjfi7553jkp7](https://forms.gle/v7oPXfjfi7553jkp7)**).**

**Additional proof is only required for achieving certain times in certain categories (see category rules to see if you need to). Regardless, when submitting a run, you agree to provide extra proof if asked by moderators. Refusal may lead to rejection.**

**If you are unsure how to submit certain pieces of additional proof, please follow the [tutorial](https://youtu.be/z2n2fCV1GY0) on submitting additional proof.**

# **External Tool Rules**

**SeedQueue, a mod that simulates multi-instance, where multiple instances of Minecraft are used to reset faster, is recommended in versions where it is available.**

- If you want to use multiple instances, such as in versions where SeedQueue is not available, please read the detailed multiple instance rules in section A.9 of the full rules.

**If you open multiple instances of Minecraft, they must each be in unique directories (separate .minecraft folders).**

**Do not use any macros in-game except for resize macros.**

- Any macros which change the screen size to within the monitor bounds may be used.
- Only one macro may make the game window larger than the monitor size, like a zoom macro for measuring Eyes of Ender. (intended to replace above rule)

**You may remap keys using external programs (like AutoHotkey), but it must be a one-to-one remap.**

- For instance, Shift+F3 cannot be rebound to a singular key.
- You may not rebind anything to the scrolling action of the scroll wheel.

**Physical reference sheets may be used, as well as four-function calculators. A reference sheet of any size not based on F3 information may be used.**

- For instance, stronghold ring locations, sheets/graphs of structure regions, and villager trading tables may be used.

**Other reference sheets and external tools must be specifically approved to be used as listed in [A.11.6 and A.11.7](https://github.com/Minecraft-Java-Edition-Speedrunning/rules/blob/132b6ffbbca78414626587b3f0d0331a3a04365e/rules.md?plain=1#L827) of the full rules.**

**Specifically approved external tools may be used, as listed in [A.11.7](https://github.com/Minecraft-Java-Edition-Speedrunning/rules/blob/132b6ffbbca78414626587b3f0d0331a3a04365e/rules.md?plain=1#L835) of the full rules. All other external tools may not be used.**

- Ninjabrain Bot for measuring Eyes of Ender is allowed.

# **Random Seed Rules**

**You are required to use a random seed (leave the seed input box blank).**

**You may not learn the seed during the run.**

- Do not do /seed until the run is over.
- Do not attempt to crack the world seed.
- After the run you should do /seed in order to include the seed in your run submission.
- Do not use F3 in pre-1.3 (it shows the seed).

# **Set Seed Rules**

**Recreate is banned in versions 1.16+.**

**You are required to set a world seed.**

# **Glitchless Rules**

**Do not save and quit or leave the game during the run.**

- You can save and quit accidentally or to resolve a bug. See the detailed rules on using Save and Quit in glitchless runs to see under what conditions it is allowed in D.1.3 of the full rules.

**A few additional techniques can be used in glitchless runs.**

- These include double-eating and Eliotex sprinting. See the detailed rules on what techniques are and aren’t allowed for glitchless runs in D.1.1 and D.1.2 of the full rules.

**SSG and RSG stand for “Set Seed Glitchless” and “Random Seed Glitchless” respectively, so they must follow the rules above.**

# **Glitched Rules**

**Glitched runs must use at least one glitch.**

- In External categories, you may Save and Quit and crash the game.

**It is highly recommended to use SpeedrunIGT in glitched categories, going to Timer, and setting the Autosave Interval to Ticks.**

**All gameplay segments are timed in glitched runs.**

**Any categories without the word “Glitchless” are glitched. This includes Any%, SS, and RS.**

# **Co-op Rules**

**Use either a dedicated** **server or Open to LAN.**

**Your server cannot use any mods that are banned, even if there are no plugins.**

- Do not use Paper, Spigot, CraftBukkit, or Bungeecord.

**You can use /difficulty to change the difficulty.**

- Do not change the difficulty in options, as it will enable peaceful momentarily.
- You must enable cheats to do this.

**If all players wait until everyone has joined, one person can do /time set 0, which will start the run’s timer.**

- You must enable cheats to do this.
- Do not use /time set 0 more than once.

**The first person to join the server, the person to complete the run, and anyone with cheats enabled must record their perspectives. When submitting your run, include these videos in the speedrun.com run description.**

- It is helpful to have all players submit a video, but only the ones above are required to.

**If more than 16 players are running, choose 16 players while submitting, input the names of 15 of the players, and then list “+others” for the 16th slot. Include the name of all other players not listed in the description of the speedrun.com submission.**

# **Structures/No Structures Rules**

**A structure is anything that requires Generate Structures: On to generate. (such as a Village, Nether Fortress, Mineshaft).**

- Dungeons are also considered a structure.
- See the full list of structures in [G.1.1](https://github.com/Minecraft-Java-Edition-Speedrunning/rules/blob/132b6ffbbca78414626587b3f0d0331a3a04365e/rules.md?plain=1#L1081) of the full rules.

**A category marked ‘Structures’ must use at least one structure.**

**A category marked ‘No Structures’ cannot use any structures.**

- You may choose Generate Structures: Off, or keep them on but do not interact with them.

# **Speedrunning Rules:**

- Escape from the map as fast as possible with the selected gamemode being either swarm or bot.

If the time is not visible, the run will be rejected. However, if a player escapes but they are not seen the run will be retimed to whenever a visible player escapes. **(REFER TO BOTTOM OF RULES PAGE FOR MORE INFORMATION)**
- FPS unlocker is allowed. Any other 3rd party extensions that assist performance (ex: autoclicker, key pressers, macros) are not allowed.
- External set-ups from previous rounds are not allowed, including spawning in with an item, abusing the crawling trap to make yourself float in the air, and spawning by the exit. The only exception would be the FOV glitch, as this may happen accidentally during all chapter speedruns.
- Any items which add adjustments to your height are not allowed unless the item is free.

# **Submission Rules:**

- As of August 5th 2024, 14:00 Pacific Standard Time, Squad Runs in Piggy and Piggy RNG no longer require 6 POVs and now **4 POVs to be verified** although, the routes listed in "Category Rules" still require a recorded POV for the run to be verified
- All top 5 runs must have a cursor present within them. This rule is for all categories, and each POV that the video is submitted with must have a cursor. (ex: if you submit a run with 3 POVs, all 3 should have a cursor present.)
- For those who double-click manually without any software/apps, you'll have to use both a click counter and audible mouse clicks as with just one it's unclear whether you are manually double clicking or using an actual macro to double click. 
- In-game audio is only required if you are using only audible mouse clicks. If a click counter is in your run, then you do not need to follow this. An asterisk (*) will be placed beside all the rules which this applies to.*

**Note: Minor exceptions can be made to all submission rules such as the run having a bad time due to a not so popular category.**

### **Solo:**

- As of July 1st, 2023 3:25 PM Mountain Standard time, **top 10 (Book 1)** and top 5 (Book 2) solo runs require either Audible mouse clicks or a click counter (Click counter must include meters, pixels, clicks and wheel ticks).[ ](https://youtu.be/oP1ZolppCeQ)https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LK1eyoL4ZyQ tutorial found here.*
- For Solo Glitch% runs, top 5 in Book 1 require click sounds or click counter, and top 3 Book 2 glitch require click sounds or click counter.*

### **Duo:**

- Top 3 Duo Runs require both players recording with in-game audio.*
- Duo world records require audible mouse clicks or click counters.

### **Trio/Squad:**

- Top 3 Trio runs require at least 2 players recording, whilst the WR needs all 3 players recording.
- Top 3 Squad runs require at least 3 players recording, whilst the WR needs at least 4 players recording.

Trio/Squad WRs require audible mouse clicks or click counter, as well as in-game audio for certain routes (Will be listed under category rules).*

**Note: Rules where there are requirements for top *X* runs does not mean the top X places, but instead the top X times. (ex: the duo world record run is a three-way tie with the time 1:31, if the next two places are 1:32, 1:33 and they must include whatever is mentioned under that category.)**



# **Run Timing Specifications**

- If a Player escaping does **NOT** have their POV, the time will be listed as the time the player's avatar disappears regardless of if the run was faster.
- If the Player escaping touches the exit at 1:00, but the timer changes to 1:01 **BEFORE THE FADE** the time of the run would be 1:01.
- If the Player escaping touches the exit at 1:00, but the timer changes to 1:01 **THE SAME FRAME** the fade occurs, the time of the run would be 1:00.
- If the Player escaping touches the exit at 1:00, but the timer changes to 1:01 **DURING THE FADE** the time of the run would be 1:00.
- If the Player escaping has a **VERY CLEAR** ping spike when they're touching the exit and they end up escaping later due to this, the time of the run would be the time they touched the exit initially.

**Note:** all of these apply regardless of the time, the times shown are just an example.

gameList.rules:
### General Rules

Full video proof with audible in-game audio is required for all submissions. Videos with extreme lag or frame drops will not be accepted.

The autosave notification ("Saving...") in the bottom left needs to be completely visible throughout the entire run.

The level must be fully loaded and visible before moving when you begin the run and you're not allowed to look around before moving to begin the run (For example, to face the gate door).

Load screen assisted jumps (AKA Enterhops) are not allowed to be used to begin a run. If it's unclear if Enterhops were used to start a run, it will be rejected.

"Jump" may NOT be bound to "Scroll Wheel Up or Scroll Wheel Down"

Framerate switching and lag abusing strategies are not allowed

All runs in the top 3 need to show FPS on the screen using the in game FPS counter. To achieve that you can see how to [bind a key to show fps in this guide](https://www.speedrun.com/outlast/guide/s6jr2)

Due to a community held vote, spamming crouch to skip cutscenes (I.E Jeremy Skip) is banned in main categories.

----

### Timing

Timing is done using the community made autosplitter/load remover which uses Time Without Loads (LRT). For help using the autosplitter/load remover, read [THIS GUIDE - CLICK ME](https://www.speedrun.com/outlast/guide/a2f0e)

If you are on PC and do not use the LRT your run will not have the loading screens manually removed, and will be verified as RTA. Loading screens are manually removed by moderators on console runs

Timing for Main Game:

Timing starts on first input after leaving Miles jeep in Administration Block. Timing ends when Miles hand touches the floor for the first time during the final cinematic in Underground Lab.

Timing for Whistleblower:

Timing starts on first input after the cell door opens in Hospital. You should start from the autosave it gives you when the cell opens but if you aren't starting from the autosave you need to get yourself into a position where you would be if you loaded the save. Timing ends when Waylon's hand touches the car handle on Miles' jeep in Exit

---

### Bhops

Bhopping is attempting to consistently get frame perfect jumps in a row, while being on the ground.

As of February 9th 2022, bhopping is banned from all full game categories on PC.

The only exceptions to this rule are :

- **"Unintentional bhops"** (as long as they are consistent on 62FPS).
Those are the bhops you can easily get without going for it because doing a jump is faster, regardless if you get a bhop or not.

- **"Strat Bhops"** (as long as they are consistent on 62FPS).
All bhops that are part of a strat are allowed. A bhop is considered a "strat bhop" if the timesave you get is not only due to the fact that bhopping is faster than running.

More information about bhop rules and examples can be found [here](https://www.speedrun.com/outlast/guides/j73iw).

All bhops are allowed on console.

---

### Game Modification

Modifying the configuration files, adding new configuration files, and using 3rd party tools that interfere with the game (Cheat Engine, Unreal Engine Mod Loaders, ect.) are not allowed.

However, there are a few exceptions:

- You are allowed to disable Steam integration. [Read this guide for more information](https://www.speedrun.com/outlast/guide/timyh)
- You are allowed to change "bPauseOnLossOfFocus=TRUE" in OLEngine.ini from TRUE to false to allow tabbing out of the game without it pausing in windowed mode. DON'T USE IN FULLSCREEN
- You are allowed to delete or rename "IntroLogo.bik" in \Outlast\OLGame\Config\Movies to skip the intro movie
- You are allowed to change "bEnableMouseSmoothing=TRUE" in DefaultInput.ini from TRUE to false
- Russian, Turkish and Hungarian fan language patches are allowed to be installed, however we really don't recommend using them as they are unsupported by Red Barrels.

----

### Additional Notes

Any major glitches, strats, and other various timesaves unknown to the community must be shared for everyone to use before the run will be verified. The strat in question must also be verified to work on everyone else's computer or consoles.

Although very rare, the moderation team may request additional proof to help with the verification process if its deemed necessary. Things we may request include:

- Split Files 
- Hand Cameras 
- Entire Attempt Sessions, Potentially Across Multiple Sessions 
- Local Recordings 

Its recommended that you keep these things and any additional proof handy with you before your run gets verified, incase we request it. If you have any additional questions, please reach out to a moderator in our Discord server.

1. All runs must be started from a **new savefile**, however the savefile may be pre-routed to a moon or have furniture moved/removed.
2. All recordings must start from the **title screen**.
3. *Save scrubbing/scum save* is **NOT allowed**.

## General Game Requirements

- Any modification done to the game outside of the in-game graphics settings is NOT allowed, unless you are running categories where FPS may be changed or wish to use the *show* commands from the 2nd rule.

- Using any console commands in any build of the game is NOT allowed. The only exceptions are: *"restartlevel"*, *"show deferredlighting"*, *"show bloom"*, *"gamma [any number from 1-5]"*, *"t.maxFPS [any number from 1-60]"*, and *"slomo 1/10/100"*. [the *"slomo (10 or 100)"* command can only be used to speed up the intro cutscenes of Alpha 1 & 4 before they end, in which you use the *"slomo 1"* to revert the game speed back to normal.] You can access those commands by installing UUU [here](https://framedsc.com/GeneralGuides/universal_ue4_consoleunlocker.htm).
- Anything that is set up or performed before a run begins that ultmately benefits you during the run is NOT allowed. (This does not include changing the resolution/window size of the game, enabling the commands LISTED in the 2nd rule, or locking the frame rate as mentioned in the last rule.)
- Any macro or script activated during a completed run is NOT allowed, unless it automates a task purely for reset efficiency with no advantage or effect on the actual gameplay (i.e. having a macro that starts a New Game for you or speeds up & slows down an unskippable cutscene is allowed).
- Mapping buttons to different ones is ALLOWED as long as they only have a maximum of 1 button per input and THAT button only has 1 input. *[Reasons why you might want a key to be bound to another one is because of a broken keyboard or because you don't like the default positions of keys the game may use (WASD, E, F, etc.)].* Also, binding a button (ex: Space, F, mouse buttons, etc.) to scroll wheel is NOT allowed as the scroll wheel acts differently from every other key and cannot be "held down" or be precisely controlled, which gives the player an advantage. (Examples include using the scroll wheel to "press" Space bar at an insane rate or to "click" the mouse buttons to quickly take off nails.)
- Any strats that abuse a change in the FPS and/or lag is ALLOWED, but the frame rate that's chosen has to be put in BEFORE the run starts and CANNOT be changed mid-run [the only method that is allowed to change FPS mid-run is by freezing the game window/process]. Keep in mind that going over **75 FPS** is banned. *[Note: "Any%: No Lag Abuse" does not allow any form of FPS or lag abuse.]*

## Media Requirements

- If anything is covering any major parts of the run such as a watermark covering a big part of the screen, your run may be rejected.

- You do not need to have a timer on the screen but it is recommended.

- In-game audio is recommended for ALL runs, but if you have only microphone audio in your video, that's okay. In addition, top 3 runs may require further evidence like the raw recording file (with audio) [the only exception to the "may" portion of the sentence are world records, which require a raw file for verification]. Runs without audio at all may be rejected if deemed too suspicious.

## Timing Regarding Loads

With loads [RTA] = From start to finish without cutting out anything.

Without loads [LRT] = Not including loads.  Loads are considered to be things like the clock screen *seen in Full Game* and the screen with the "LOADING..." text *seen in Alpha 4 and the betas*.
