### Important Rules:

- Avatars that contain any body parts bought with robux for an advantage are not allowed for use in non-limitless speedruns. This also includes the usage of paid emotes as well as UGC and off-sale packages.
- Physics-affecting text within Roblox’s engine is not permitted and will be rejected on sight. This includes major visuals-affecting text, such as Bloxstrap’s GUI Remover. 
- **You must display your FPS with any means necessary (Shift F5, Microprofiler).** In normal (non limitless) runs, going above 60 fps is not allowed. This will be enforced.
- Being stuck in certain states (squid animation, line launcher animation) is fine however if abused will result in your run being rejected.
- Clips of any sorts where you phase through a part of the map are not allowed in non-limitless categories. This includes climb clipping, emote clipping, line launcher clipping, etc.
- Squid related tech such as squid skip, squid drop, and squid pushing are currently not permitted due to uncertainty regarding if they are patched or not. The only squid tech currently allowed is squid bouncing.
- Fishing for tier 4 items in Isle is not permitted in non-limitless categories to help with the prominent issues of RNG.

### Portals:

The "Portals" sub-category separates runs that use the in-game RNG teleportation from runs that don't. This includes the use of the strange rock. Mandatory portals (such as at the end of Snake's Lair and in the Mantis crater) are not included when defining a portal for this sub-category. The Teleporter device will not count a run as a portals run as it is a manually placed device and is not RNG dependent unlike portals.

### Limitless:

Everything that is normally banned is permitted in Limitless (EXCEPT for paid/event modifiers, UGC/off-sale packages, and speed glitching) such as FPS unlockers, paid emotes/parts etc. Anything goes. If you are a part of the Badorkbee server or the Roblox group, please be aware that runs under this subcategory are NOT competitive and therefore will NOT award badges, roles, titles, etc.

### Timer:

Time starts exactly on the first frame when the screen blacks out at the opening cutscene and ends exactly on the first frame at a run's end. The timing for the end of the run will be defined for each category.

In-Game Time refers to the timer within the Isle game which can be activated within the settings and can be added as a second method for timing. However, the first timing method is used as the default timing method and therefore will be exhibited as such in regards to the leaderboard. Do not add an In-Game Time to your run if you are not using the Timer setting within Isle.

### Video:

The entire run, from start to finish (before the black screen until after the end of the run) has to be shown in one single video (no cuts/splices, separated footage, etc.) with in-game audio and must be of acceptable quality. In-game audio should be loud/clear enough to be heard over any background noise you may have.

### Modifiers:

Modifiers are not considered a "subcategory" and runs with legal modifiers will be on the same board against runs without them. Paid/event modifiers are not allowed in non-limitless and limitless categories. Modifiers that disable badges are not allowed in non-limitless categories, such as:

- Isle 8 
- Team Battle 
- Radio Comms 
- Free Camera 
- No Death Return 
- Rolling
- Fish Life, etc.

This list excludes "Speedrun Mode" even though it is a badge disabling modifier as Speedrun Mode is intended for its express use within speedrunning.

### Multiplayer rules:

1. Footage must be recorded from both players, following the same video rules from above. In a multiplayer run, only one person needs to trigger the necessary criteria to end/’start’ the run. This includes starting the fuel pump or activating an exit.
2. Please place the link to the second video in the description when you submit a run. Preferably embed.
3. Any runs submitted with over two players in-game will not be accepted.

gameList.name: Portal
gameList.rules:
# **Goal**

Beat the game without scripts, macros or cheats.
This has to be done in one sitting, quicksaves and quickloads are allowed.

# **Version**

For Portal runs the Source Unpack is used which can be found in the [resource section](https://www.speedrun.com/portal/resources), you can do runs on the latest Steampipe but note that not all tricks will be usable (mainly saveglitch).

# **Timing**

Timing begins when the crosshair appears and ends when it disappears after Glados' death.
PC timing is done using In-game time. LiveSplit is highly recommended due to its auto-start/stop and load removal. All runs using in-game time must be using the newest version of SourceSplit.
Console runs are retimed manually by verifiers to be load removed time. Milliseconds are removed from console runs to keep timing consistent.
You are allowed to use the official save from the [resource section](https://www.speedrun.com/portal/resources) to skip the vault.
Pauses have to be timed (Engine Ticks with Pauses in the autosplitter settings).

# **Proof and submitting**

*All runs HAVE to be submitted with some sort of proof in form of a video or demos.* In case of suspicion demos can be requested by the mods.
Videos have to show the full run from start to finish. Video must be hosted on a permanent video platform that embeds on speedrun.com, such as Youtube, or a Twitch Highlight. You may also submit using bilibili, even if it does not embed properly. Temporary platforms such as Streamable or your Twitch VOD are not acceptable. If you are submitting Time without loads with only video proof, the video has to show Livesplit comparing against Gametime throughout the entire run, with at least the first two decimal places visible (1:23.45 is acceptable, 1:23.4 is not).
For runs in the top 25, game audio is required; otherwise, game audio is required if video is the only form of proof.
Demos can automatically be recorded with [Maxxuss' demo plugin](https://github.com/RedHaze/speedrun-demo-record-unified). Runs cannot be submitted with only demo proof if the game is paused mid-run.
Runs that would end up in the top 25 have to be submitted with a live video and demo proof.
Runs that would end up in the top 100 have to be submitted with demo proof, with video proof being optional, but encouraged.
sv_unlockedchapters must be set to 0 before the run starts if New Game is to be used.

# **Whitelist**

Allowed commands/bindings:

- Any bind that is accessible from the menu 
- sv_player_funnel_into_portals binding (checkbox in the menu) 
- toggle_duck binding (default controller bind) 
- cl_showpos 1 
- r_drawviewmodel 0
- binds for sensitivity 
- save/load on one key binding 
- save, fps_max [fps], load on one key binding
- custom named save binds 
- demo plugin related binds 
- toggle binds
- viewmodel_fov
- say related binds (example: bind 7 "sv_player_funnel_into_portals 0; say funneling off")
- gl_clear 1
- net_graph 1
- cl_showfps 1
- sv_autosave 0
- mat_dxlevel 80/90
- echo

You are allowed to use multiple commands on one bind, as well as aliases. Regulations for these can be found [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1WB4ZWGoOVUBcy-rO2KeUk9WyQhgXM5gDwMRShrDXQp4/edit?usp=sharing), and not following them will invalidate your run.

As of 7/7/2023: SST version 0.5 is now allowed in runs.
You can use it to:

- Set your FOV to any value between 75-120
- Use record to have ongoing demos; instead of speedrun_start / speedrun_segment
- Use it to customize your portal crosshair colors 
- Change DPI scaling 

You CANNOT use it to:

- Have binds that change Portal colors during the run

As of 17/03/2025 Ghost door in 05 is banned, as this is only possible due to actions before the start of the timer. Previous fullgame runs will be grandfathered in, and previous IL runs will be rejected.

Any wall or floor texture changes are not allowed. Other texture and sound file changes are allowed as long as they would not give an advantage. Cosmetic and size changes for fonts in "SourceScheme.res" are allowed. Saving and loading repeatedly to intentionally progress the game without the timer moving is not allowed, however specific strategies that utilize this (such as BSG or save delay) are allowed.

Copymap is banned.

No plugins other than Maxxuss' demo plugin, SST and the input hud plugin are allowed to be loaded during runs.

If you are unsure about a command, bind or other rule please ask via the [discord](https://discord.gg/Tvk9zP3) or the [forum](https://www.speedrun.com/portal/forum).

Tutorials on how to set everything up as well as strats can be found in the [Ultimate Portal Speedrun Guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1H7AHqiSTRzJE2xfqPCGBsUXZay1g9wdUfCbPXoz8S3c/edit) (embedded link).

Rules:

1. All CubeCraft rules must be followed. To view these rules, visit: https://www.cubecraft.net/rules.

2. **Players who attempt to fake runs will receive a 6-month ban from CubeCraft Speedrunning. A second offense will be a permanent ban. A permanent ban will result in the removal of all a player’s runs from CubeCraft Speedrunning, even if they’re legitimate runs. Bannable offenses include, but are not limited to: having a friend snipe your game to help you get a faster time, sniping a friend of yours to get on the same team as them in a no party run, having a friend join your game and leave after the game starts, lessening the number of players you need to kill on order to win, and using a hacked client to give yourself a faster time.** If you have questions on whether or not something is bannable, please contact a page moderator!

3. If a player who has submitted runs is permanently banned on CubeCraft Games for cheating (after the submission/verification of their runs), their runs will be removed from the page if we can not verify they were not cheating in the runs (e.g. we do not have their POV of the run). 

4. Runs where players ask their opponents to do something (e.g. leave the game, void themselves, etc.) will be rejected. Do not ask players on opposing teams to do something to improve your time.

5. Players are required to show themselves entering the game, either by going through the portal/map selection menu or by queuing into a new game after the previous game has ended using the compass.

6. Runs must be unedited and uncropped. Runs with cuts in the video footage or sections of the screen covered or missing will be rejected. The entire run must be recorded from start to finish in order to be verified. Screenshots or partial recordings will not be accepted.

7. If there is a hacker present in your game that contributes to your game in any way, the run will be rejected.

8. Live streaming while speedrunning is discouraged. If an individual submits a run that takes place during a live stream, it will not be accepted.

9. Runs that take place on seasonal maps–maps that are only present on CubeCraft for a short period of time throughout the year–can not be accepted for the overall leaderboard. However, you are welcome to submit runs on these maps to the “individual level” leaderboard.

10. Timing starts when the "Let the games begin!" message appears in chat and ends when the "(your name) won the game!" message appears. Runs will not be timed using the in-game timer due to its inaccuracy.

11. At least 50% of players must be present at the start of the game. Along with this, if a game starts with 50% of players, no other players may leave after the start of the game.

12. When submitting a run, only select the platform you are playing on.

- Mods or hacks of any kind are banned.
- Modifications to the Switch that give unfair advantages are banned.

### Timing

- Timing begins upon pressing the big yellow button ("OK" in most languages) to start the first race.
- Timing ends upon crossing the finish line of the final track.
- Submit your RTA time in the “Time” field. **Leave “In-game Time” blank!**
- Cup runs must begin on the first track of the cup (i.e., you may not submit cup runs done in the middle of a longer run).
- 16 Tracks or 48 Tracks runs done within a larger run may be submitted. In this case, timing begins upon crossing the finish line of the final track before the category and ends as normal. For example, a Bonus Tracks run contained within a 48 Tracks run would start upon crossing the finish line of N64 Rainbow Road and end upon crossing the finish line of Big Blue.

### VS Race Rules

- Some rules vary between categories, but these rules are always consistent:
- Teams: No Teams
- COM: Any COM for No Items Runs, Hard COM for Items Runs *(Implemented Nov. 13, 2023)*
- COM Vehicles: All Vehicles
- Cup items runs may be done in Grand Prix mode rather than VS mode.

### Proof

- All submissions for 48, 32, and 16-track categories faster than the following threshold times (see below) must include video proof. The first time is the threshold for runs on the digital version; the time in parentheses is the threshold for the cartridge version, which loads more slowly. (Implemented 8/15/20)
- *NOTE: The minimap must be clearly visible (not covered by splits or other visuals) to qualify as adequate video proof.*
- If a Twitch video is used, it must be a HIGHLIGHT, NOT a vod. Twitch automatically deletes stream vods after two weeks.

- For all Cup categories, times within 10s of the world record (RTA) require video proof.
- Handheld and camera recordings are acceptable.

### Other Rules

- Only single-player speedruns are allowed.
- Auto-Accelerate is allowed.
- Smart Steering is allowed, although using it for full runs is discouraged.
- Again, submit your RTA time in the “Time” field. **Leave “In-game Time” blank!**
- If your video proof features multiple attempts or runs, please leave timestamps for the start and end of your run. If we have to spend time trying to find out where your actual run is, we may reject it and ask you to resubmit

gameList.rules:
*Go to ``Category Rules`` for rules dependent upon this category.*

# General Rules

- You must play on sm64coopdx (PC/Android Build of sm64ex-coop are not allowed as of August 2nd 2024)
- **You must show the Server Settings before starting your run**, this simplifies our verification process a lot. You can that by recording them before hosting or do it in-game by pausing, pressing R then selecting Server Settings.

# Starting a run and retiming

- The players must start on the beige circle that Mario would jump onto upon jumping from the pipe in the intro cutscene. See picture if not specific enough: [Starting Circle](https://imgur.com/a/9yrAkgR). If any player is not on this circle as the run begins via countdown, the run is deemed invalid.

- Time ends when a player grab the Grand Star

# Host Settings

- The save slot used for a run must be at 0 Stars

### Under "*Settings*"

- **Player interaction** must be set to **Solid**
- **Knockback Strength** must be set to **Normal**
- **Stay in level after star** is dependent upon the category, turn off if on Vanilla, rather than non-stop, and vice versa
- **Bouncy Level Bounds** must be set to **Off**
- **Skip Intro Cutscene** can be set to **Enabled** or **Disabled** (Enabled is recommended)
- **Pause Anywhere** can be set to **Enabled** or **Disabled** (Enabled is recommended)
- **Bubble on death** can be set to can be set to **Enabled** or **Disabled**
- **Nametags** can be set to **Enabled** or **Disabled**

### Under "*Mods*"

- We recommend using the Speedrun Timer Reworked mod which can be found in **Resources**
- For 1P runs, you are allowed to use the "Singleplayer Pause" mod found in **Resources**
- **Character Select mods are currently banned** (still in discussion)
- If it is a mod that changes the HUD in some way (E.g. a speedrun timer, countdown, etc.) and doesn't change the gameplay (E.g. changing a character's moveset, allowing the player to spawn objects, automatically spawning stars) then you can have it enabled.
- Speed Display is **banned**
- All other mods must be **disabled**
- **DynOS packs** are **allowed**

# Submission and Number of POVs Requirements

- The video submitted must have game audio at all times. If there are several videos, then at least one of them needs it.

- All submissions can contain only one POV as long as it doesn't meet a time threshold, which you can find in ``Category Rules``

#### **If you meet the time threshold**

- You must submit the recordings of at least half of the players. If there is an odd number of players, then the majority. (E.g. 3P, 2 POVs). **If the submission is 2P, submit both POVs.**

- Even if you *don't think* you'll meet the time threshold, please have the correct amount of people recording in case you do.

## Extra Notes

- If the game has a network shutdown, that's fine. The timer will be paused and once all players are back into a game together on the same file, the timer will be resumed. The castle cannot be entered until all players have joined.
- If only one person crashes, have them join back. The timer will not pause during this time.
- Character selection (as well as palette) is not important, as all characters have the same framework and functionalities, just different player models.
- Unlike Super Mario 64 Online using Net64, not all players need to be in the final Bowser Fight. It's recommended that someone who is recording be in the Bowser Fight, otherwise we won't know when the run has ended.
- If a player joins the run who was not in it when it began, you can kick them or ask them to leave. If they enter the castle, the run is deemed invalid.
- If someone accidentally activates Lakitu before beginning, you can still perform the run on that file. It barely saves any time, probably one second, which is too insignificant for it to matter.

- Runs with strategies designed around the use of limited time global buffs (such as Solstice Empowerment) will be rejected.
- Strategies exploiting the game's connection-based nature will be reviewed for consistency between fireteams of different player compositions before being permitted.
- Exploits or strategies that Bungie has expressed the intention to patch or have precedent in being patched by Bungie are not permitted until it is clear that they will remain in the game.
- Any glitch listed in [this forum post](https://www.speedrun.com/destiny2/forums/pnnuu) is not allowed in any run.
- For information on artifact mod bans, please see [this thread](https://www.speedrun.com/destiny2/forums/v95ms).

# Submission standards

- Video proof of the entire duration of the run for at least one encounter POV and one POV for each out-of-bounds/skip player is required for all runs. 
- Runs that do not use the activity completion banner as their end condition must demonstrate that the strategy being employed in the run would result in a successful activity completion.
- Supported websites include YouTube, Twitch, and bilibili.
- For top 3 submissions, the POV of the player that makes the first input affecting the run's time is required, and the run will be timed based off of this POV in order to avoid discrepancies.
- Moderators reserve the right to retroactively reject or remove runs where submitted video evidence is deleted, made private, or otherwise inaccessible.
- Corrupted gameplay or gameplay obscured or impacted by overlays may be rejected (non-intrusive overlays such as DDT and threepole are permitted).

# Starting conditions

- Starting with any weapon equipped is allowed, provided that it is not fired or prepped in any way (Lament cannot be charged, Izanagi's Burden cannot be honed, Eager Edge cannot be active, etc.).
- Any run utilizing an ability that a player would not have if they had started the activity immediately upon load-in may be rejected at verifier discretion.
- Valid starting positions are limited to where a player could randomly spawn upon loading into the activity (read category rules for exceptions).

# Timing

- Runs generally end on one of the five following conditions (see category rules for exceptions):

1. Boss healthbar flash/death
2. First frame of mission complete banner
3. First frame of mission summary line
4. Last frame of level visible
5. Frame after interact is filled (empty circle)

  ![](/static/blob/kzwo3d8e.png)

- After cutscenes and loading screens, timer resumes on either the first input that affects the run or optionally when the level becomes visible for the player with the slowest load.
- Runs with strategies involving wipe screens or rejoins will have wipe screens equalized to 17s in raids and 7s in dungeons and levels (timed from leaderboard black screen to first visible spawn frame), while rejoins will be equalized to simulate perfect load times (equalization specifics can be found in category rules).

For more information on category-specific rules, check the individual category rules by clicking "Show rules" at the top right corner of a leaderboard. If you have further questions, feel free to head to our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/d2speedrun).

# Game Engine Rules

- All runs must be played on the most recent version within the Hitman: World of Assassination (2021) game engine. (Renamed from Hitman 3)

# General Video Guidelines

- Run must be posted somewhere that is unrestricted (no sign-in required to watch) and permanent (no expiration date).  Please use one of the following platforms if possible:
-       YouTube (Preferred)
-       Google Drive (Click Share -> Get Link -> Anyone on Internet can View)
-       Bilibili (Mostly for Chinese users)
- If video proof of the run is not watchable later for any reason, the run may be removed at moderator discretion.
- Videos may not be edited such that parts of the video are sped up or cut together.
- Otherwise suspicious runs with video skips/other visual anomalies including but not limited to frame drops, significant ghosting, excessively low bitrate, **or similar audio anomalies including but not limited to missing or inaudible in-game audio** will be rejected at moderator discretion.
- Videos must maintain a level of viewability and the majority of the screen must be uncovered. Rating screen must be fully visible.

# Submission Guidelines

- All video submissions should START before the level or during the beginning cutscene and END with the rating screen.
- All speedruns must have SA, Difficulty and Timer HUD enabled/visible. Mini-map HUD is optional, but encouraged.
- SA and SA/SO submissions require a 5-star rating screen on Professional or Master difficulty, otherwise it will be relabeled as Any%. Any% speedruns can be played on any difficulty.
- All speedruns are timed and sorted by LRT (Load Removed Time) NOT RTA (Real TIme Attack). RTA can be included for full-game submissions, but should be left empty for ALL individual level runs.
- Most run submissions should NOT include ms, however if a world record time is tied 4 (or more) times our moderation team will convert that LB to ms. All runs with ms will be double checked by our moderation team regardless if you add the ms in your submission.
- ALL speedruns submitted with a time under 7 seconds will be required to press 'P' on the rating screen to show the score breakdown. This will allow us to accurately calculate ms for speedruns like Freeform Training Any%. 
- **Camera FOV scaling via resolution stretching to the point where you can shoot through walls is not allowed.**

# Fullgame Resetting

- Any resets between starting the level and the rating screen (including cutscene) will have a 1 second minimum penalty. After 1 second the penalty is equivalent to the time on the in-game timer when you restart the level. (Ambrose explosion bug on spawn is an exception and will not result in any penalty for restarting)
- Bangkok and all Sarajevo Six levels carry a higher minimum penalty of 10 seconds to negate the advantage gained from spam restarting the level.

# NG+ vs NG Explanation

- Note that all runs (including "any%") on this leaderboard are New Game Plus runs due to historical demand, and difficulty resetting progress in this game for a true New Game experience. For something coming close to New Game speedruns, check out "Default Loadout" here: [https://www.speedrun.com/hitman_woa_extensions](https://www.speedrun.com/hitman_woa_extensions)

# Game Modifications Policy

### Allowed

- **[Peacock](https://thepeacockproject.org/wiki/intel) is Allowed (Peacock plugins/mods are NOT allowed)**
- Crosshair overlays that don't affect the in-game crosshair are permitted, but direct modifications to the in-game crosshair are banned. It is necessary for moderators to be able to see that the in-game crosshair has remained unaltered. If moderators can not prove that the in-game crosshair is unaltered, moderators can reject the run at their discretion.
- Third party FPS capping software (such as RivaTuner) may be used, but you cannot change your FPS mid-run with third party software. 
- Changing your FPS mid-run with the in-game graphics options (such as Vsync or Super Sampling) is allowed.

### Not Allowed

- **All Mods.** (as of Nov. 2024 rule change)
- Non-visible/non-game changing mods don't need to be uninstalled, but must be inactive during the run (ex. freecam and path tracer)
- Any third party cheat tools such as WeMod.
- Any macros that bind multiple actions to one button or key.
- **[Ansel Freecam](https://rentry.org/hitman3ansel)** (you can use it for routing and practice, but cannot be active during runs).
- **[Using Ansel to skip dialogue](https://youtu.be/z2-yAqbZu-8?t=94).**
- **Nvidia Profile Tweaker** (Tweaking the games visuals beyond the extent of the in-game settings menu via third party tools such as nvidiaprofileinspector, or editing the game's .ini files will not allowed)
- Resolution scaling past the boundaries set by the game in order to shoot through walls.

# General Etiquette (not a rule)

- **There is an informal expectation within the Hitman community to credit inspirations for your strategies. Please consider giving credit to anyone's strategies that influenced your run, whether that be in speedrun.com run description or in Youtube video description etc.**

The following is prohibited:

- All versions of Zsnes are banned.
- All versions of SNES9x before 1.5 are banned. If you insist on using SNES9X, please use the most recent version.
- Retroarch's "Run-Ahead to Reduce Latency" feature is banned.
- Nakitek Game Saver and other third-party hardware additions, that alter the way in which the game is read by and written to the console, are banned. Exceptions to this include SD2SNES, Super UFO, Everdrive, and USB2SNES so long as adequate power is supplied to the console and the game functions as it would normally.

- The platform that the player chooses must not be altered in any meaningful or significant way, or change the interactions between system and game that exist or are emulated. Any changes must be entirely aesthetic - functional or practical changes to systems are not allowed. Therefore, S-Video, RGB, Component, and similar modifications to the signal outputted from the console are allowed. Disclaimer: although the dejitter mod designed by marqs85, souce code seen here, alters the clock rate of the game and is as such subject to this rule, it does so at such a minute rate (less than 2 frames per hour LOST by the mod compared to original), that it has been deemed acceptable by the community at large for use.
- Modifications to the game’s ROM — including but not limited to changes to the game’s code, the appearances of sprites within the game, or the game’s music — are prohibited.
- Neither the CPU nor any other chip can be overclocked.
- Currently, permitted emulators and settings are not objectively superior to the original hardware for speedrunning purposes. Therefore, the native settings - or those preferred by other speedrunners - are approved.
Any sort of savestate feature is banned, including Virtual Console restore points, the SNES Classic's Rewind, and savestates of the SD2SNES/FXPAK. Observing the state of the console or emulator is allowed for the sake of functions like autosplitters or input display, but cannot be used in any way to gain an advantage.
- Submitting an emulator movie file or a recording of an emulator movie file playing is not allowed. Video submissions must be of live gameplay recorded through software or through an actual camera pointed at a tv or monitor.
- Attempting 30Hz Arm Pumps to execute Bomb Torizo skip on the NTSC version of the game is banned.

The input device rules are as follows:

- Each button used on the controller must correspond one-to-one to a button on the SNES controller.
- The use of macros or turbo is prohibited, even if the controller has this functionality built in.
- The use of Left+Right or Up+Down simultaneously on the directional pad is banned for all categories unless explicitly stated otherwise. On hardware that allows simultaneous Left+Right or Up+Down inputs, intentional abuse of the system used to prevent Left+Right or Up+Down (SOCD resolution) is not allowed.

# **Speedrunning Rules:**

- Escape from the map as fast as possible with the selected gamemode being either swarm or bot.
- The timer used will be the in-game timer. The time of your run starts in-game, and ends the frame your screen starts to fade. The timer must be clear to see when the player escapes. If the time is not visible, the run will be rejected. However, if a player escapes but they are not seen the run will be retimed to whenever a visible player escapes. **(REFER TO THE BOTTOM OF THE RULES PAGE FOR MORE INFO)**
- FPS unlocker is allowed. Any other 3rd party extensions that assist performance (ex: autoclicker, key pressers, macros) are not allowed.
- External set-ups from previous rounds are not allowed, including spawning in with an item, abusing the crawling trap to make yourself float in the air, and spawning by the exit. The only exception would be the FOV glitch, as this may happen accidentally during all chapter speedruns.
- Any items which add adjustments to your height are not allowed unless the item is free.

# **Submission Rules:**

- As of August 5th 2024, 14:00 Pacific Standard Time, Squad Runs in Piggy and Piggy RNG no longer require 6 POVs and now 4 POVs to be verified although, the routes listed in "Category Rules" still require a recorded POV for the run to be verified.
- All top 5 runs must have a cursor present within them. This rule is for all categories, and each POV that the video is submitted with must have a cursor. (ex: if you submit a run with 3 POVs, all 3 should have a cursor present.)
- For those who double-click manually without any software/apps, you'll have to use both a click counter and audible mouse clicks as with just one it's unclear whether you are manually double clicking or using an actual macro to double click. 
- In-game audio is only required if you are using only audible mouse clicks. If a click counter is in your run, then you do not need to follow this. An asterisk (*) will be placed beside all the rules which this applies to.*

**Note: Minor exceptions can be made to all submission rules such as the run having a bad time due to a not so popular category.**

### **Solo:**

- As of July 1st, 2023 3:25 PM Mountain Standard time, top 10 (Book 1) and top 5 (Book 2) solo runs require either Audible mouse clicks or a click counter (Click counter must include meters, pixels, clicks and wheel ticks).https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LK1eyoL4ZyQ tutorial found here.*
- For Solo Glitch% runs, top 5 in Book 1 require click sounds or click counter, and top 3 Book 2 glitch require click sounds or click counter.*

### **Duo:**

- Top 3 Duo Runs require both players recording with in-game audio.*
- Duo world records require audible mouse clicks or click counters.

### **Trio/Squad:**

- Top 3 Trio runs require at least 2 players recording, whilst the WR needs all 3 players recording.
- Top 3 Squad runs require at least 3 players recording, whilst the WR needs at least 4 players recording.
- Trio/Squad WRs require audible mouse clicks or click counter, as well as in-game audio for certain routes (Will be listed under category rules).*

**Note: Rules where there are requirements for top *X* runs does not mean the top X places, but instead the top X times. (ex: the duo world record run is a three-way tie with the time 1:31, if the next two places are 1:32, 1:33 and they must include whatever is mentioned under that category.)**



# **Run Timing Specifications**

- If a Player escaping does **NOT** have their POV, the time will be listed as the time the player's avatar disappears regardless of if the run was faster.
- If the Player escaping touches the exit at 1:00, but the timer changes to 1:01 **BEFORE THE FADE** the time of the run would be 1:01.
- If the Player escaping touches the exit at 1:00, but the timer changes to 1:01 **THE SAME FRAME** the fade occurs, the time of the run would be 1:00.
- If the Player escaping touches the exit at 1:00, but the timer changes to 1:01 **DURING THE FADE** the time of the run would be 1:00.
- If the Player escaping has a **VERY CLEAR** ping spike when they're touching the exit and they end up escaping later due to this, the time of the run would be the time they touched the exit initially.

**Note:** all of these apply regardless of the time, the times shown are just an example.

gameList.rules:
- ***A video of your run is required in your submission.*** Brief periods of missing video as a result of reloads are permissible as long as the audio is clear and intact throughout. The video must include both the start of the run and the end of the run, except as specified in the category rules. *All videos from Twitch, including highlights and VODs, are not allowed.*

- ***You must start with a 0-reset fresh save file.*** All files in the save directory, except for "config.ini", must be deleted before initiating a run. A guide to finding this directory can be found here: https://pastebin.com/pjcNLQAj. The in-game "True Reset" mechanic does not delete the save files, so it does not count for this requirement.
    - Starting the run with system_information_963 in your save folder (called "soulless" which happens after selling your soul following a genocide run) is permitted in any categories where it doesn't give an advantage. This includes Neutral, True Pacifist, Genocide, and any other single-ending categories, as soulless is equal or worse in these categories. Categories where soulless is not allowed at the start of the run include True 100%, Soulless Pacifist, and Soulless Genocide.
- ***Any edits to the data.win file, in any way shape or form, is an automatic disqualification.*** The only modifications allowed to the game in any capacity are:.
    - Modifications to the .ogg music files in your Undertale directory
    - Removal of steam_api.dll.
    - Running a linux version of the game on a windows operating system by renaming a linux game.unx to data.win and optionally patching an undertale.exe using the provided patches in the resources section
    - Renaming a data.win file (for example having a normal and a debug data.win with different names run through different shortcuts)
    - Unpacking a 1.0 version of the game
    - Modifications to the options.ini file
    - Modifications/removal of splash.png
    - Modifications to credits.txt except in categories that get no-hit Special Thanks or otherwise use credits.txt during the run
- ***Editing or deleting save files during a run is forbidden.*** Reloading to a save file created prior to the start of the run is not allowed. Dying to force a reload to a save file created prior to the start of the run is also not allowed.
- **If any pre-run setups are performed (such as RNG manipulation), the game and category rules apply as soon as the first game client is opened.** Otherwise, the game and category rules apply as soon as timing begins.
    - Pre-run setups, if performed, must also be included in the submission video starting from as soon as the game can be captured.

- ***All IL runs and any sub-hour 1.0-1.001 neutral runs will have milliseconds listed.*** It is not necessary for runners to include the milliseconds themselves on submission

- ***Multi-client is forbidden.*** You can have additional clients open on the main menu for optimal load times, but you cannot interact with an older client after loading a save file (pressing "Continue") with a newer one. An autosave counts as an interaction even if no player input was involved. Closing a client does not count as interaction.
    - Photoshop Flowey fight special rules:
        - Due to the lack of a main menu in the Photoshop Flowey fight, during that instance, you cannot interact with an older client after interacting with a newer one. The Photoshop Flowey fight is defined as starting from when Flowey force closes the game and autosaves (when file8 is created) to ending when the UNDERTALE logo appears after touching the door and the game autosaves.
        - You cannot interact with any clients loaded prior to the autosave that starts the Photoshop Flowey fight after the autosave happens. If you accidentally load a client too early or load a client during a game-write and as a result break this rule, it is okay so long as you immediately close the client and do not interact with it.
        - If you leave the client where you killed Flowey open too long and as a result this client creates an autosave after you've interacted with a newer client, it is allowed as long as your only interaction with this old client or any clients that load this save file is touching the ending door. This exception is intended to allow the runner to reload their normal save file if they accidentally allow this autosave to take place. The ending resulting from this interaction does not count towards category requirements and runs that abuse this exception will be rejected.

- ***External tools must not interface directly with the game.*** This includes reading the game memory or save files. They must also not read data from the game window (e.g. reading the colors of specific pixels) except in a blind manner, such as displaying a screenshot of the game in a different window. External tools may read inputs from the mouse, keyboard, and controller including keypresses that are sent to the game. However, external tools may not attempt to simulate gameplay using game inputs.
    - Autosplitters and automatic kill counters are exceptions to this rule. Autosplitters must not read information that would be unknown to the runner.

- ***Any use of macros to control the game is banned***, with the exception of using a hotkey to start the game and using the half-speed automash mod available in the Resources tab. ***No other automashers or macros are permitted*;** this includes features built into keyboard firmware or driver software such as onboard macros, Snap-Tap and other forms of null-bind, Dynamic Keystroke, and other similar features.
- ***The following key rebinds are the only allowed external key rebinds:***
    - Binding the arrow keys to WASD and/or IJKL. You can only bind up to W/I, left to A/J, down to S/K, and right to D/L. You are allowed to use the arrow keys in addition to WASD/IJKL.
    - Moving the keys Z, X, and C within the leftmost 7 letter keys on the bottom row of the keyboard (Z, X, C, V, B, N, and M on a QWERTY keyboard). The three keys must be in the order Z, X, C from left to right and must be on three consecutive keys. You are only allowed to use one key for each of Z, X, and C.
    - Moving the keys Ctrl, Shift, and Enter to the keys /, ', and ]. You can only bind Ctrl to /, Shift to ', and Enter to ]. If you use this key rebind, you must rebind all three keys. You are only allowed to use one key for each of Ctrl, Shift, and Enter.
- ***Any external key rebinds other than the ones listed above are banned.*** Key rebinds done within the game through the Controller/Joypad setup menu are allowed.

- ***Only one version of the game may be used in a run.***

All runs require video proof (with audio).

It is recommended that every submitted video that includes Daylight Saving Time Abuse (DSTA) start by showing Daylight Saving Time (DST) being set prior to starting the run.

Use of Amiibo, 2P, Luigi's Balloon World, and Assist Mode are banned, unless a category explicitly states otherwise.

Runs performed on emulator will not be verified (switch hardware only).

Runs must be done entirely with your switch in docked or undocked mode, you may not switch between the two mid run.



**Breaks**

If your run uses breaks, choose TA for the Method variable. If it doesn't, choose RTA.

Both start and end of every break must be timestamped in the run description.

Breaks are only allowed during cutscenes; this includes moon animations.

When taking a break, runners should bring up the menu to edit the system time while synchronization with the internet is turned off. This is to ensure that enough time has passed outside of breaks for a seed to be fully grown and the moon to be collected. This option is under "Date and Time" in the switch settings menu. Make sure to confirm the system time with an "A" press at the end of your break so it remains the same as it was at the start of the break.

The pool of available time for breaks gains 15 minutes every 2 hours. Breaks can be taken at any point in the run, and there is no limit on the number of breaks so long as it follows the rules established above.

For example:

- Any run under 2 hours cannot take any breaks.

- Any run between 2 and 4 hours (2:00:00 - 3:59:59) has 15 minutes available for breaks.

- Any run between 4 and 6 hours (4:00:00 - 5:59:59) has 30 minutes available for breaks.

- etc.

Breaks are calculated based on the final run time, so if a runner knows that the run will be over 2 hours they can use from the 15 minute pool instantly. Should mistakes be made, and the run did not hit the required threshold to allow breaks (or did not hit the required threshold to use the amount of break time taken), the run will be retimed.

# HELLDIVERS 2 GENERAL RULES

**Before submitting**: please check the **category-specific rules** by:

1. Opening the **leaderboard**,

2. Choosing any **"full game"** run or **"level"** run,

3. Going to **Rules - Category rules**.

All runs require **video proof**.

## Ban/violations

- The use of **macros** is **banned**.

- The use of **aiming sights/reticule mods** is **banned**.

- **Host transfer** (a tactic where the host leaves in the middle of the game) is **banned**.

- Runs with up to **4 players** are **valid**. The tactic of more than four players **taking turns** during a run is **banned**.

- The use of **DSS** (Democracy Space Station) and **Free Stratagems** is **banned**.

- You may submit a run with a **Free Stratagem** as long as **no runner uses it**. If a **Free Stratagem** is **available**, **all POVs** must be submitted.
- You may submit a run done in a planet with the **DSS** as long as it has **all POVs** submitted on the run and **no stratagems** or other **benefits** provided by the **DSS** are **used**. You can also check to see if the **DSS** is **inactive**, in which you can also submit your run if shown on video. To do so, open the **DSS menu** from the **galactic map**. The message "*There is currently no active action*" must be displayed, as shown below:

![](/static/blob/xzdpwj5z.png)

## Submission guideline

- You may **dual submit** a run to **Extract%** and **100%** if the time is **competitive** in **both categories** (World Record contender).
- You may **dual submit** a run to **Extract%** ([main page](https://www.speedrun.com/Helldivers2)) and **Extract% Deathless** ([category extensions page](https://www.speedrun.com/HELLDIVERS_2_Category_Extensions)) if the time is **competitive** in **both categories** and if the **Deathless requirements are met** (see any [Deathless category rules](https://www.speedrun.com/HELLDIVERS_2_Category_Extensions/leaderboards?h=blitz-search-and-destroy-100-deathless-terminids-10-super-helldive-multiplayer-standard&rules=category&x=l_dno5o37w-wdmjoq5d-0nwm9v58.qyzy5731-j84j2y48.192955jq-rn1y25dn.1py044e1-p85y26xl.qke4999q)). You may proceed in the **same way** for runs that can be submitted in both **100%** and **100% Deathless** categories.
- You may **not dual submit** to **Any%** and **Extract%**/**100%**.
- You may **dual submit** clips of **full game runs** as a **separate video link** to the **individual level categories**.

- For missions with neither **outposts** nor **secondary objectives** where **extraction** is the only thing to do after **completing** the **main objective**, submit to **100%** instead of **Extract%**.

## Rules for Verifiers

Verifiers may ask for **additional POVs** before verifying in **certain circumstances**:

- Competitive times in competitive categories,

- Illuminate missions,

- Abnormalities, etc.

Verifiers may **not self-verify** runs.

## Community Guidelines

Do not **save up** runs to post them all at once for dramatic effect. Hitting a lot of runs in one day and posting them **is ok** but **hoarding** runs **is not**.

## Standards of Proof

Every run requires the **score screen** to be part of the video.

![](/static/blob/kzwrq0re.jpg)

You may submit the **In-Game Time** shown in the **score screen**.

**In game audio** must be **recorded** and set to an **audible level**. **In game music** and **voice chat** is **optional**.

![](/static/blob/1n5358jz.png)

**Mission timer** must be set to **always visible**. To do so, go to: **Settings > HUD > Mission info visibility**, set it on **visible**. Note that this is **not** the **default setting**.


**First time** submitters will be given a **single** instance of leniency regarding the timer visibility rule and the run will be manually retimed for validity. Runner will be given a warning and all future submissions without timer set to always visible **will be rejected.**

![](/static/blob/1n7j6mln.jpg)

The **stratagem and stuff selection screen** as well as the **loadout screen** must be **shown** before the run starts.

## How to find category-specific rules

![](/static/blob/1n578qje.png)

# 1. Modding

1.1 **MODDING, CHEATING AND HACKING OF THE GAME IS STRICTLY NOT ALLOWED!** If your game states "Mods Detected" in the middle, your run is considered invalid. This rule also applies if it is evident or suspected that the game files have been changed or altered. 
1.1.1 The only exception to rule 1.1 are runs which have taken place in an official  tournament setting (hosted by or with permission from the SRC Mod Team).
1.2 This also includes using tool assistants like TAS or macros.
1.3 Any bugs or glitches you may happen to know are allowed. This excludes bugs or glitches which have been disallowed by the leaderboard mods.
1.4 The current and only exception is removing fog from the game via the .ini file

# 2. Timer and score

2.1 The timer starts as soon as the player gains control and ends on the rating screen.
2.2 All runs must use the in-game timer given at the rating screen, unless the category rules say otherwise.
2.3 **ALL RUNS MUST INCLUDE THE WAITING SCREEN PRIOR TO THE RUN STARTING AS WELL AS THE FULL SCORE SCREEN (INCLUDING LETTER SCORE) AT THE END OF A RUN!**
2.4. All runs must include the milliseconds given by the in-game timer, unless specified otherwise by the category rules.

# 3. Recording

3.1 All runs require video proof uploaded on platforms like YouTube or Twitch.
3.2 The game has to be in focus all the time, alt-tabbing out of the game is only allowed before and after the run.
3.3 All runs require original game audio. 
3.3.1 Runs without audio and/or significant visual issues may be verified at the moderators discretion.
3.4 **MULTIPLAYER RUNS MUST BE SUBMITTED WITH EACH PLAYER'S POV.** i.e. If you are playing duo, both players POVs are to be submitted on the one run submission. This is to verify that client side mods are not in use by each individual player.
3.4.1 Runs submitted before the implementation rule 3.4 (29 JAN 2025) will be grandfathered. No action will be taken against existing submission that do not meet rule 3.4.

4.1 Provide as much information as possible when submitting your runs. This includes the amount of players you have played with, which players you have played with, the timing, etc.
4.2 Runs submitted by moderators will not be self-verified. The only exception to this is, if the runs have been unverified for 21 days and upwards.

This is because this shield allows you to move slightly faster than the other riot shield, and since it was a supporter edition only item (which is now unobtainable) we feel as if a pay to win shield simply isn't fair. 
5.2 Each specific category has its own unique rules, please read them as well to check what the submission requirements are for each category!

gameList.rules:
#### Welcome to SA2B Speedrunning!

### Listed below are descriptions of concepts, terms and rules that you may need to understand each Category’s individual rulesets.

##### IGT and the Autosplitter

- Several categories are ranked based on their Time Without Loads (Loadless) as displayed by the game. 
- On PC, there is an Autosplitter that tracks your Loadless automatically. More info here: http://www.speedrun.com/sa2b/guide/fabjo
- On Console, or if you’re unable to use LiveSplit’s Autosplitter functionality, you need to calculate your Loadless manually. More info here: http://www.speedrun.com/sa2b/guide/uw9lv

##### File Types [NG/NG+]

- New Game and New Game+ are differentiated by the type of file that they are completed from. A New Game run must be completed from a Fresh File, while a New Game+ run must be completed from a Completed File.
- A “Fresh File” is a newly created File that does not have any progress made on it. In order to set up a Fresh File, one must do so in the Settings, or the File Select Screen.
- A “Completed File” is one that has already been made, and therefore already has made progress in the game. This means that any upgrades are allowed, you may start with more than 4 lives, and Stage Select can be fully unlocked, as well as any alternative Karts or Costumes.

##### Thresholds

- In order to increase the accessibility of the game’s most popular categories, video is often not required until a runner’s pb reaches a certain benchmark. Due to speedrun.com’s organization system, any run that has Loadless will be placed above every run that does not. For this reason, we remove the Loadless of all runs that do not surpass the Threshold, regardless of if they are submitted with Loadless, so that the leaderboard remains properly ordered at every rank. Each category’s Threshold can be found in their Rules.

##### Video Requirements

- Runs that require video would ideally be submitted via a website such as YouTube. Twitch VODs and Clips are allowed as well, but due to past issues YouTube is preferred.
- Please refrain from uploading your video proof to websites such as Streamable, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter, Facebook, etc. as they are not accessible in all regions and may get automatically deleted after some time has passed.

##### Frame Rate

- The game should be played as close to 60fps as possible. If the run has significant frame drops the Mod Team reserves the right to reject it.

##### ISO Loading

- For console categories that use loadless: using a USB/SD card loader, an optical drive emulator, or playing on a burned disc is allowed.
- If playing on a Dreamcast with a burned disc, all 3CD versions and the 1CD version from DCRes are allowed.

##### Banned Strats

- Taking long, unnecessary breaks in untimed sections such as cutscenes and upgrades could void your run.
- 3rd-party controllers are banned from use on the Dreamcast version of the game.
- If using Quick Save Reload, using the prompt reset version mid-run to skip menuing to the file selection screen in Options is not allowed.
- Some strats have a significant effect on the speedrun, and may sometimes encourage play that goes against the spirit of the category. For this reason a list of Banned Strats exists on every category’s Rules page.
- A list and explanation of every banned strat and what they mean can be found here: https://pastebin.com/qmXuGxqB
- Additionally, closing the game at any point in time to gain an advantage (besides to deactivate ESG) could void your run.
- Finally, we reserve the right to reject any run that does not technically break any rules, but does something deemed objectionable.

##### External Software

### The following mods/software are allowed for use during speedruns of all categories:

- SA2ModManager’s “Pause When Inactive”, “Disable exit prompt”, "Disable loading animation" & "Skip Intro" (in the Options tab)
- Input Displays made by Jelly & OnVar
- Autosplitters downloaded via LiveSplit or otherwise approved by moderators
- skewbmaster's SA2 Quick Save Reload mod
- IDGeek121's White Jungle No Rain mod
- Sora-yx's Error Message Fixes mod
- F-Man's 50% SFX Volume mod
- Onvar's Dreamcast deadzone fix

## Downloads to all of these can be found in the Resources tab.

### The use of Upgrade Remover, or other similar mods, is banned mid-run. If a player has acquired upgrades that they shouldn’t have at a given point, or there is other evidence of external mods/software affecting the run, the submission will be rejected.

##### Emulators

### Dolphin Emulator is allowed for the boards. Please see our rules for Dolphin below:

1. Only NTSC versions of SA2B are accepted.
2. Dolphin version 5.0-17995 must be used. (https://dolphin-emu.org/download/dev/8bad821019721b9b72701b495da95656ace5fea5/)
3. The window's title bar showing the emulator version, framerate, etc. must be visible in the video.
4. Emulator must run at full speed. An occasional lag spike is fine, but consistent slowdown is not.
5. "Speed up Disc Transfer Rate" must be disabled. (Right-click SA2B -> Properties)
6. "Enable Emulated CPU Clock Override" must be set to 100% or turned off completely. (Config -> Advanced)
7. "CPU Emulation Engine" must be set to "JIT Recompiler for x86-64" (Config -> Advanced)
8. "Skip EFB Access from CPU" must be unchecked. (Graphics -> Hacks)
9. Modifications, cheats, editing .ini files and emulator exclusive functions are not allowed.
10. Using save states as an alternative to resetting manually is not allowed.
11. Emulator is only allowed for Main Board Story Categories and Individual Levels.

Note: Any of the emulator rules shown above may be changed and retro-actively applied if new information about emulation is found that would require a rule change.

Video proof is required. Please use Livesplit or another timing method to measure the run time and do your best to manage the time yourself. However, a timer is not required for runs but is recommended to get the general time of your speedrun. Run mods will retime runs as required by category.

**Submission Rules:**

For multiplayer runs, the point of view of all those participating in the run is required. An exception to this rule is the Diluvian Mechanism category. Runs that do not submit the POVs of all those participating will be promptly rejected.

Runs submitting something other than a run of the game like a random YouTube video or image will be autorejected and reported for spam.

Please upload your run to YouTube so that it can be retimed manually without a download and run through editing software.

Abusing loopholes in speedruns will result in your run being rejected.

If your run is still processing, it can be added to the queue. Moderators will wait until your run is processed before verifying.

Runs submitted to the leaderboard should be unedited. This means that submissions that include intentional or unintentional obstructions on screen so that your player's build cannot be seen will be rejected. An exception to this rule is adding a timer in-post as long as it does not obstruct crucial details on screen.

Runs should clearly show effort in attempting to get a good time. Runs that intentionally stall or are intentionally slow to get a slow time will be rejected.

Stalling in runs such as waiting many minutes for a reset or to get a specific Crazy Slots weapon before movement is not allowed.

gameList.name: Super Metroid
gameList.rules:
The following platforms are allowed:

- The original Super Famicom and Super Nintendo Entertainment Systems, as well as the New-Style Super NES clone systems, are classified as SNES (colloquially as 'console').
- The Nintendo Wii, Wii U, and 3DS Virtual Consoles are classified as WiiVC, WiiUVC, and 3DSVC respectively.
- The Super NES Classic Edition is classified as SNESClassic.
- Permitted emulators such as Retroarch, SNES9x, higan/bsnes, lsnes, and Bizhawk are classified as SNES[Emu]. The latter two are primarily used for tool-assisted speedrunning and are not recommended.
- Unclassified clone consoles should be considered emulators until further notice.

The following is prohibited:

- All versions of Zsnes are banned.
- All versions of SNES9x before 1.5 are banned. If you insist on using SNES9X, please use the most recent version.
- Retroarch's "Run-Ahead to Reduce Latency" feature is banned.
- Nakitek Game Saver and other third-party hardware additions, that alter the way in which the game is read by and written to the console, are banned. Exceptions to this include SD2SNES, Super UFO, Everdrive, and USB2SNES so long as adequate power is supplied to the console and the game functions as it would normally.

- The platform that the player chooses must not be altered in any meaningful or significant way, or change the interactions between system and game that exist or are emulated. Any changes must be entirely aesthetic - functional or practical changes to systems are not allowed. Therefore, S-Video, RGB, Component, and similar modifications to the signal outputted from the console are allowed. Disclaimer: although the dejitter mod designed by marqs85, souce code seen here, alters the clock rate of the game and is as such subject to this rule, it does so at such a minute rate (less than 2 frames per hour LOST by the mod compared to original), that it has been deemed acceptable by the community at large for use.
- Modifications to the game’s ROM — including but not limited to changes to the game’s code, the appearances of sprites within the game, or the game’s music — are prohibited.
- Neither the CPU nor any other chip can be overclocked.
- Currently, permitted emulators and settings are not objectively superior to the original hardware for speedrunning purposes. Therefore, the native settings - or those preferred by other speedrunners - are approved.
Any sort of savestate feature is banned, including Virtual Console restore points, the SNES Classic's Rewind, and savestates of the SD2SNES/FXPAK. Observing the state of the console or emulator is allowed for the sake of functions like autosplitters or input display, but cannot be used in any way to gain an advantage.
- Submitting an emulator movie file or a recording of an emulator movie file playing is not allowed. Video submissions must be of live gameplay recorded through software or through an actual camera pointed at a tv or monitor.
- Attempting 30Hz Arm Pumps to execute Bomb Torizo skip on the NTSC version of the game is banned.

The input device rules are as follows:

- Each button used on the controller must correspond one-to-one to a button on the SNES controller.
- The use of macros or turbo is prohibited, even if the controller has this functionality built in.
- The use of Left+Right or Up+Down simultaneously on the directional pad is banned for all categories unless explicitly stated otherwise. On hardware that allows simultaneous Left+Right or Up+Down inputs, intentional abuse of the system used to prevent Left+Right or Up+Down (SOCD resolution) is not allowed.
- External objects may be held by a runner for stability or comfort, however no external objects are allowed to physically make inputs for the player during the run, unless there is a valid accessibility reason for doing so.

gameList.name: Sonic 3 & Knuckles
gameList.rules:
For Full game runs, you are required to play Sonic 3 locked-on to Sonic & Knuckles or an appropriate ROM file, For ILs you are allowed to use either Sonic 3 locked-on to Sonic & Knuckles, or just Sonic & Knuckles.
Runs submitted from the following games are not permitted:

- Sonic the Hedgehog 3 (standalone)
- Sonic & Knuckles (except for ILs)
- Sonic & Knuckles Collection
- Sonic Origins
- Other ROM hacks or releases (e.g. prototypes, Sonic 3 Complete, Sonic 3 AIR etc)

# General Rules

- When playing as Sonic & Tails, any input on the second controller voids the run, except if the category specifically allows it (i.e Co-op/1p2c).
- Abusing the Data Select screen to manipulate emerald counts is banned.
- The use of debug mode is banned in all categories.
- Level select is banned in all full game categories.
- Level select is allowed in IL (Individual Level) categories, but the use of the frame advancing features of the pause menu is banned.
- Game audio is required and must be synchronized and at an audible level throughout the run.
- Whilst PAL is allowed, it will be held to a higher scrutiny in ILs and maybe rejected if a run is deemed to contain a competitive advantage when using PAL (trick precision, etc). PAL is only allowed when using real mega drive hardware.

# Timing Rules

For ILs, timing is done using the In Game Timer. However, if the run is not continuous, all time spent within the stage (such as deaths) shall be added together.

For Full-game runs, timing is to be done with real time minus the time bonuses from each level (place this time in the Real Time column) starting from selecting your character and ending when the screen fades to white just before the final cutscene starts. Submissions must show at least the first portion of the final cutscene following the fade to white to show the game has been beaten.

If you do not know how to time this, simply submit your full real time, make a note of it in the comment, and a moderator will take care of it for you.

# Pre Manipulation

Unless stated in category rules, no pre-run memory manipulation is allowed.

# Wrong Warps

Wrong warping of any kind is only allowed in relevant categories, and is banned in regular categories.

# Emulator Rules

The following unofficial emulators are allowed:  Kega Fusion 3.64, Genesis Plus GX (standalone or through Retroarch.) Links to these emulators can be found in the Resources tab.  The emulator must run at full speed.

It is strongly recommended that the emulator used is adequately identifiable at some point during the run (preferably at the start).
Your run may be rejected if the emulator cannot be identified from the video and is suspected of not being ran on a valid emulator and/or core.

## Examples 

### Fusion (only 1 needed)

- FPS Visible in the bottom of the window.
- Text in the bottom right either showing:
    - Soft Reset
    - Hard Reset
    - x Startup (where x is either "Genesis", "MegaCD" or "Master System")  

### Retroarch

- Showing the Retroarch Menu that displays the Genesis Plus GX core and version in the bottom left.

If not shown at the start of the run, please provide a timestamp in the run description of where this is shown.

# Savestates

For Full-game runs, the use of save states at any point during the run will void the run.
For IL (individual level) runs, save states may be used to return to a point before the transition to the level starts, but not during or after the run.

# Analogue Mega Sg Rules:

For runs using the Analogue Mega Sg, the Mega Sg's main menu screen (the screen with the "Run Cartridge" option) and its buffer options screen must be shown before a run. The game must be visibly reset before a run. If using the "Zero Delay" buffer option, RTA time will be corrected to make up for the speed discrepancy the option creates.

# Disabling Super/Hyper Music

For NG+ and All Emeralds use of the following codes are allowed to keep the stage music:

Codes:

- disable hyper sonic music: REPA-C6YR (PAR: 011A8E:4E71)
- disable super tails music: RFJT-C61Y
- disable hyper knuckles music: RF6T-C6V0
- transformation music stays off after cut scenes: RFPT-T6YC (PAR: 085B82:4E71)
